chemistry/acids-bases.8b7b6a08379d: Memory hint: Below seven equals acidic. The lower the number, the more acidic.
chemistry/acids-bases.7c40d94f71f1: Baking soda solution. pH eight point three. Basic. Baking soda, sodium bicarbonate, is a mild base. It neutralizes acids — and fizzes with vinegar, giving off carbon dioxide.
chemistry/acids-bases.4f6d10b54274: Antacid, milk of magnesia. pH ten point five. Basic. Antacids are bases that neutralize extra stomach acid to relieve heartburn. Stomach acid, hydrochloric acid, has a pH of about one point five to three point five.
chemistry/acids-bases.064778f8cb5f: Seawater. pH eight point one. Basic. Seawater is slightly basic, about pH eight point one. As the ocean absorbs C O two from the air its pH slowly drops, ocean acidification, which harms shells and coral.
chemistry/acids-bases.6a7c14360a82: Memory hint: Low number equals lots of hydrogen ions equals acid.
chemistry/acids-bases.8d562653caf9: The pH scale. Measures acidity from zero to fourteen. pH runs from zero, most acidic, through seven, neutral, to fourteen, most basic. pH tells how many hydrogen ions are in a solution: the more hydrogen ions, the lower the pH. Each step is a times ten change: pH three is ten times more acidic than pH four and one hundred times more acidic than pH five.
chemistry/acids-bases.e184573b3a70: Household ammonia. pH eleven point six. Very basic. A base used in glass cleaners. Never mix ammonia with bleach — it makes a toxic gas!
chemistry/acids-bases.c336a86b3864: Battery acid. pH zero point eight. Very acidic. Car batteries contain sulfuric acid, H two S O four. It is corrosive: it can burn skin and eat holes in clothing.
chemistry/acids-bases.e0ff77f9b800: Neutralization. Acid and base react to form salt and water. When an acid and a base react, hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions join to make water: hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions react to form H two O. The other ions form a salt. Example: H C l and N a O H react to form N a C l and H two O. If equal amounts react, the solution ends up neutral, pH about seven. Everyday uses: antacids for heartburn, soapy water on itchy insect bites, formic acid, and slaked lime to fix acidic soil.
chemistry/acids-bases.bbf80f09ec63: Base. pH above seven. Bases release hydroxide ions in water. They taste bitter and feel slippery, like soap. Bases turn red litmus blue and turn phenolphthalein pink.
chemistry/acids-bases.9cc1cbcbd5e9: Milk. pH six point six. Acidic. Milk is almost neutral, just slightly acidic. When milk goes sour, bacteria make lactic acid and the pH drops.
chemistry/acids-bases.7240d67993f4: Tomato. pH four point three. Acidic. Tomatoes are mildly acidic — that’s why tomato sauce tastes tangy.
chemistry/acids-bases.336f94954620: Lemon juice. pH two point two. Very acidic. Citric acid gives lemons their sour taste. A sour taste is a property of acids.
chemistry/acids-bases.f916e5576f44: Neutral. pH equals seven. A neutral solution is neither acidic nor basic: pH seven. Pure water is neutral because it has equal amounts of hydrogen ions and hydroxide ions. Salt water and sugar water are neutral too.
chemistry/acids-bases.9778f511b625: Memory hint: Above seven equals basic. The higher the number, the more basic.
chemistry/acids-bases.42c0e979639a: Black coffee. pH five. Acidic. Coffee is only weakly acidic. Normal rain is also slightly acidic, about pH five point six, because carbon dioxide from the air dissolves in it.
chemistry/acids-bases.5c8859da73e1: Drain cleaner. pH thirteen point eight. Very basic. Contains sodium hydroxide, lye, one of the strongest common bases. It dissolves hair and grease in pipes — and can badly burn skin and eyes.
chemistry/acids-bases.f982345e658d: Pure water. pH seven. Neutral. Pure, distilled, water is neutral: pH seven at twenty-five degrees Celsius. It has equal amounts of hydrogen and hydroxide ions. Tap water is usually between pH six point five and eight point five.
chemistry/acids-bases.44b77ef48edc: Acid. pH below seven. Acids release hydrogen ions in water. They taste sour, lemons, vinegar — but never taste lab chemicals! Acids turn blue litmus paper red and purple litmus solution red. Many acids react with metals such as zinc to make hydrogen gas.
chemistry/acids-bases.2c8ad37733d1: Memory hint: Seven sits in the middle of zero to fourteen, like the middle of a seesaw.
chemistry/acids-bases.c7640a907e4f: Vinegar. pH two point nine. Very acidic. Vinegar is about five percent acetic acid in water. It is used for cooking, pickling and removing hard-water scale.
chemistry/acids-bases.bce4997f28f6: Orange juice. pH three point five. Acidic. Contains citric acid and ascorbic acid, vitamin C. Lemon juice is about twenty times more acidic, at pH two point two.
chemistry/acids-bases.be71458c666b: Bleach. pH twelve point six. Very basic. Bleach, sodium hypochlorite solution, is strongly basic and a powerful disinfectant. Bases feel slippery because they react with the oils on your skin.

chemistry/atoms.262fcdf767dc: Neutron. Neutral particle in the nucleus, with zero charge. Charge: zero. Mass: about one atomic mass unit, a tiny bit heavier than a proton. Neutrons help hold the nucleus together. Without them, the positive protons would push each other apart. Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons are called isotopes.
chemistry/atoms.3fb186243859: Nucleus. The tiny, heavy center of the atom. Made of protons and neutrons packed tightly together. Holds more than ninety-nine point nine percent of the atom’s mass, but only a tiny part of its volume. If an atom were the size of a football stadium, the nucleus would be about the size of a pea at the center. The nucleus has a positive charge because of its protons.
chemistry/atoms.43dd1909ec37: Electron. Negative particle around the nucleus, with a charge of minus one. Charge: minus one. Mass: about one over one thousand eight hundred thirty-six of a proton, so it barely counts toward the mass. Electrons are arranged in shells around the nucleus. The shells are energy levels. In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons. Electrons in the outermost shell take part in chemical reactions. These are the valence electrons.
chemistry/atoms.da8361adfee6: Atomic number. equals number of protons. Every element has its own atomic number: H is one, C is six, O is eight. The periodic table is arranged in order of atomic number. In a neutral atom, it also equals the number of electrons.
chemistry/atoms.de81465ff36c: Mass number. equals protons plus neutrons. Electrons are so light that we don’t count them. Neutrons equals mass number minus atomic number. Example: carbon fourteen has fourteen minus six equals eight neutrons. The number after an element’s name is its mass number, as in carbon twelve.
chemistry/atoms.3e30816245c1: Common mix-up: The third shell can actually hold eighteen electrons, but for the first twenty elements it holds eight before the fourth shell starts.
chemistry/atoms.7396bc35da59: Schrödinger and others. Electron-cloud, quantum, model. Electrons do not follow exact paths. We can only say where they are likely to be: a fuzzy electron cloud. In nineteen thirty-two Chadwick discovered the neutron, completing today’s picture. Experiments showed that electrons behave like waves as well as particles.
chemistry/atoms.428f222e73d5: Electron shell. Energy levels where electrons are found. For elements one to twenty: shell one holds up to two electrons, shell two up to eight, shell three up to eight, the two-eight-eight rule. Electrons fill the inner shells first, then move outward. Atoms with a full outer shell, like helium, neon and argon, are very stable and unreactive.
chemistry/atoms.e232784686e1: Proton. Positive particle in the nucleus, with a charge of plus one. Charge: plus one. Mass: about one atomic mass unit, A M U. The number of protons is the atomic number, and it decides WHICH element the atom is. Add or remove one proton and the atom becomes a different element. Try it!
chemistry/atoms.7e493199129c: Electron cloud. Today’s model: where electrons are LIKELY to be. Scientists cannot know exactly where an electron is at any moment, only where it is likely to be. Where the cloud is thicker, the electron is more likely to be found. This quantum, cloud, model came from scientists such as Schrödinger in the nineteen twenties.
chemistry/atoms.02b72df6be1b: Ion. An atom with unequal protons and electrons. Lose electrons, more protons than electrons, positive ion, cation, for example, sodium ion. Gain electrons, more electrons than protons, negative ion, anion, for example, chloride ion. Table salt is made of sodium and chloride ions held together.
chemistry/atoms.5c7b59fd782b: Isotope. Same protons, different neutrons. Carbon twelve, carbon thirteen and carbon fourteen are all carbon: each has six protons. Some isotopes are radioactive, unstable. Carbon fourteen is used to find the age of things that were once alive, up to about fifty thousand years old. Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium, zero neutrons, deuterium, one neutron, and tritium, two neutrons.

Cutting an object in half halves both the mass and the volume, so its density stays the same.

chemistry/elements-compounds.18613adceb15: Common mix-up: N H three is not flat. Nitrogen also has a pair of unshared electrons on top, which pushes the three H atoms down into a pyramid.
chemistry/elements-compounds.ebfa33402985: Table salt, sodium chloride. Compound, pure substance. Ions stacked in a crystal. Sodium ions and chloride ions attract each other and stack in a repeating cube pattern called a crystal lattice. There are no separate N a C l molecules. The formula gives the ratio: one N a for every one C l. Sodium is a soft metal that reacts violently with water, and chlorine is a poisonous gas. Bonded together, they make the salt you eat! Salt grains are little cubes because the ions stack like cubes.
chemistry/elements-compounds.b7c9cb9ad6a3: Carbon dioxide. Compound, pure substance. A straight-line molecule. One carbon atom sits between two oxygen atoms in a straight line, one hundred eighty degrees. Each C equals O double bondlink is a double bond. You breathe out C O two; plants take it in for photosynthesis. “di” means two: carbon DIoxide has two oxygens.
chemistry/elements-compounds.408b75c54594: Common mix-up: Sand is mostly the compound S i O two and iron is an element, but mixing them does not make a new compound.
chemistry/elements-compounds.99da708bd1c7: Common mix-up: The four belongs only to H, not to C. C H four does not have four carbons.
chemistry/elements-compounds.c4a6b020cbc6: Sand and iron filings. Heterogeneous mixture. You can see the parts. You can see the different parts: tan sand grains and gray iron bits. One spoonful might have more iron than another. The mixture is not the same everywhere. A magnet pulls out the iron because iron is magnetic and sand is not. Mixtures can be separated by physical means. Heterogeneous equals “different” parts you can see or pick out.
chemistry/elements-compounds.729aa574553f: Oxygen gas. Element, pure substance. Only one kind of atom. Made only of oxygen atoms, so it is an element, a pure substance. Two oxygen atoms share electrons in a double bond to form one O two molecule. About twenty-one percent of the air is O two. You need it to breathe, and fires need it to burn. Element equals only ONE kind of atom, even if the atoms are joined in pairs.
chemistry/elements-compounds.2f3562e6a19c: Iron. Element, pure substance. A metal made of single atoms. Iron is an element: every atom in it has twenty-six protons. Metal atoms are not grouped into molecules. They pack together in a repeating crystal. Iron is magnetic, which helps us pull it out of mixtures. Symbols: first letter CAPITAL, second letter lowercase. F e comes from the Latin word “ferrum”.
chemistry/elements-compounds.31b77b4067a8: Common mix-up: O two is a molecule, but it is NOT a compound. A compound needs two or more DIFFERENT elements.
chemistry/elements-compounds.36be04f9576e: Ammonia. Compound, pure substance. A pyramid-shaped molecule. One nitrogen atom bonds to three hydrogen atoms. The molecule is a short pyramid with N at the top, H N H about one hundred seven degrees. Ammonia is used to make fertilizers and is found in some cleaners. It has a strong smell. N H three: one Nitrogen, three Hydrogens.
chemistry/elements-compounds.6eb9c3f09f7a: Air. Homogeneous mixture. A mixture of gases. Air is about seventy-eight percent nitrogen, N two, twenty-one percent oxygen, O two, almost one percent argon, A r, plus a tiny bit of C O two, about zero point zero four percent, and water vapor. The gases are mixed evenly but are NOT bonded to each other. Each keeps its own properties. The amounts can change: a crowded room has more C O two, and air near the ocean has more water vapor. Mixture equals substances mixed but not bonded; the “recipe” can change.
chemistry/elements-compounds.d72334c81049: Methane. Compound, pure substance. A tetrahedron-shaped molecule. Methane is the main part of natural gas, used for cooking and heating. The four hydrogen atoms point to the corners of a tetrahedron, one hundred nine point five degrees apart, as far from each other as possible. Carbon usually forms four bonds. That is why it can build so many different molecules. No subscript means one: C H four equals one C plus four H equals five atoms.
chemistry/elements-compounds.cdb4b5844075: Common mix-up: Air contains O two and N two molecules, but air is not a compound. There is no single formula for air.
chemistry/elements-compounds.1f609ad9f51d: Common mix-up: C O, carbon monoxide, “mono” equals one, is a different, poisonous gas. One oxygen atom makes a big difference.
chemistry/elements-compounds.aa558d7439db: Water. Compound, pure substance. Two hydrogen and one oxygen, bonded. Two elements, hydrogen and oxygen, are chemically bonded, so water is a compound. The molecule is bent: the H O H angle is about one hundred four point five degrees. Every water molecule has the same two to one ratio of H to O. A compound always has a fixed ratio. Water is totally different from its elements: H two burns and O two helps fires, but water puts fires out! A subscript counts the atom just before it: H two O equals H double bond, H, O.
chemistry/elements-compounds.b4db0a0fee68: Common mix-up: H two O two, hydrogen peroxide, is a different compound. Change a subscript and you change the substance.

chemistry/reactions.ae251210f84c: Common mix-up: You need two O two, not one: the products contain four O atoms, two in C O two plus one in each H two O.
chemistry/reactions.2ba34c04cbef: Methane burns. Combustion. Methane, natural gas, burns in oxygen. This is the flame on a gas stove. The products are carbon dioxide and water vapor, both invisible gases. Count: one C, four H and four O on each side. Mass: eighty atomic mass units, eighty atomic mass units. In an open kitchen the gases drift away, so it looks like the fuel just disappears. Burn something made of C and H in O two and you always get C O two and H two O.
chemistry/reactions.5a4984868b89: Hydrogen burns. Synthesis, combustion. First the H single-bond H and O double-bond O must break. Then the atoms regroup: each O atom bonds to two H atoms, making two H two O. Count: four H and two O before, four H and two O after. Mass: thirty-six atomic mass units, thirty-six atomic mass units. This reaction releases lots of energy. It powers some rockets and fuel-cell cars. Atoms are like LEGO bricks: take the model apart and build something new. Same bricks, new shape.
chemistry/reactions.1906bccc613b: Making ammonia. Synthesis. Nitrogen and hydrogen join to make ammonia, which is used to make fertilizer. The strong triple bond in N two is hard to break, so factories use heat, high pressure and a catalyst. Count: two N and six H on each side. Mass: thirty-four atomic mass units, thirty-four atomic mass units. Four molecules become two molecules, but the number of atoms stays eight. Molecules can change in number. Atoms can’t.
chemistry/reactions.0f1e3b3d9d19: Common mix-up: The two in front of H two O is a coefficient, two molecules. Writing H two O two instead would make a different substance: hydrogen peroxide!
chemistry/reactions.383759796717: Splitting water. Decomposition. Electricity splits water into hydrogen gas and oxygen gas: the reverse of hydrogen burning. Two water molecules react to form two H two and one O two. Count: four H and two O on each side. Mass: thirty-six atomic mass units, thirty-six atomic mass units. One reactant breaking into simpler substances is called decomposition. Decomposition: one thing, two or more things.

chemistry/solutions.14cfa57e52ba: Solution. A mixture that is the same all through. Solution equals solute and solvent. It is a homogeneous mixture: the same everywhere. Solutions are transparent, see-through, even when colored, like blue copper sulfate solution. The solute never settles out of a solution, no matter how long it sits. Mass is conserved: mass of solution equals mass of solute plus mass of solvent.
chemistry/solutions.2d234a0385aa: Memory hint: Solute and Solvent equals Solution.
chemistry/solutions.4d7ae81b49ec: Common mix-up: Dissolving is not melting! Melting needs heat to turn a solid into a liquid; dissolving is when solute particles spread out between solvent particles. The sugar’s mass doesn’t vanish: one hundred grams of water plus twenty grams of sugar equals one hundred twenty grams of sugar water.
chemistry/solutions.a76bef3c9066: Solubility. The most that can dissolve. Solubility is the maximum mass of solute that dissolves in one hundred grams of solvent at a given temperature. At twenty degrees Celsius, one hundred grams of water dissolves about two hundred four grams of sugar but only about thirty-six grams of table salt. Solubility is a physical property — it can help identify a substance. For most solids, solubility increases as temperature rises.
chemistry/solutions.bbe84bf0467d: Memory hint: Solubility always comes with a temperature: “thirty-six grams per one hundred grams of water at twenty degrees Celsius”.
chemistry/solutions.5e90cdd48613: Particle size. Smaller pieces dissolve faster. Crushing a solid into powder gives it far more surface area touching the solvent. Granulated sugar dissolves faster than a sugar cube, but the same total mass dissolves in the end. Cutting one cube into eight smaller cubes doubles the surface area.
chemistry/solutions.a61b609da4ad: Common mix-up: Divide by the mass of the solution, solute plus solvent, not just the water.
chemistry/solutions.67d4bfc17069: Temperature. Speeds dissolving and changes solubility. Hot water particles move faster, so they hit the solid more often and with more energy. For most solids, a higher temperature means a higher solubility: K N O three goes from about thirty-two grams at twenty degrees Celsius to one hundred sixty-nine grams at eighty degrees Celsius. Salt barely changes: about thirty-six grams at twenty degrees Celsius and thirty-eight grams at eighty degrees Celsius. Gases are the opposite: they dissolve less in warm water.
chemistry/solutions.399d11f40f3d: Concentration. How much solute is in the solution. Concentration tells how much solute is dissolved in a certain amount of solution. Mass percent equals mass of solute divided by mass of solution times one hundred percent. Example: twenty grams of sugar in one hundred grams of water, twenty divided by one hundred twenty, about sixteen point seven percent. Concentrated equals lots of solute; dilute equals little solute. Adding water dilutes a solution. With a colored solute such as copper sulfate, a more concentrated solution looks darker. Try it!

chemistry/states-of-matter.5ce71fb892e4: Melting. Solid, liquid, heat is absorbed. Ice melts at zero degrees Celsius. This is its melting point. While melting, the temperature stays at zero degrees Celsius until all the ice has melted. The energy breaks the lattice apart. Melting one gram of ice takes three hundred thirty-four joules of energy.
chemistry/states-of-matter.25fe7eb4beca: Sublimation. Solid, gas, skipping the liquid, heat is absorbed. Particles at the surface of a solid escape straight into the gas. Dry ice, solid carbon dioxide, sublimates at minus seventy-eight degrees Celsius: it never becomes a puddle. Snow can slowly disappear on cold, sunny, dry days without melting.
chemistry/states-of-matter.7651119ecf3b: Temperature. How fast the particles move on average. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the particles. Kinetic energy is motion energy. Hotter equals particles move faster. Colder equals particles move slower. At absolute zero, minus two hundred seventy-three degrees Celsius, particle motion is at its lowest possible level.
chemistry/states-of-matter.1d4bcef7d5f2: Freezing. Liquid, solid, heat is released. Water freezes at zero degrees Celsius, the same temperature at which ice melts. Particles slow down until attractions lock them into a lattice. Freezing releases heat. Farmers spray water on fruit trees on frosty nights so the freezing water protects the fruit.
chemistry/states-of-matter.ebd6e8aa3f6f: Water molecule, H two O. The tiny particle that makes up water. All matter is made of tiny particles, atoms or molecules, that are always moving. Each water molecule is one oxygen atom, red, joined to two hydrogen atoms, white. Ice, liquid water and steam are made of exactly the same molecules. Only their spacing and motion change.
chemistry/states-of-matter.6b49bc7ed8d2: Common mix-up: Changing state is a physical change. No new substance forms: H two O stays H two O.
chemistry/states-of-matter.bba515ba816c: Vaporization, boiling and evaporation. Liquid, gas, heat is absorbed. Evaporation happens only at the surface and at any temperature. That is how puddles dry up. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at the boiling point: one hundred degrees Celsius for water at sea level. Boiling one gram of water takes two thousand two hundred sixty joules, almost seven times more than melting it!

china/ancient-engineering.754ae78524c7: MORTISE and TENON. Dovetail tenon. A tenon shaped like a swallow’s tail, dropped in from above. Through tenon. Dovetail. The tail is wider at the end, so once it drops in, the beam cannot be pulled out sideways. Clever: the harder you pull, the tighter it locks. china/beijing-capital.fc342b33f7a3: Wanning Bridge. The oldest bridge on the axis, twelve eighty-five. First built in twelve eighty-five in the Yuan dynasty, and still used by traffic today. china/beijing-capital.dd8afaf75939: Tian’anmen. Gate of Heavenly Peace. Built in fourteen seventeen as the front gate of the Imperial City, and given the name Tian’anmen in sixteen fifty-one. On October first, nineteen forty-nine, the founding ceremony of the People’s Republic of China was held here. It appears on China’s national emblem.

china/beijing-capital.50468213efaf: The park wall is round in the north and square in the south: “round heaven, square earth”, 天圆地方.
china/beijing-capital.e4dafbf1ddee: Beijing and Washington, D.C., are almost the same distance from the equator, yet their climates differ. Their latitudes are thirty-nine point nine degrees north and thirty-eight point nine degrees north, respectively. Hover over the charts to see each month.
china/beijing-capital.1cd238df1077: Screen wall, 影壁. Blocks the view from the gate. A decorated wall just inside, or opposite, the gate. Visitors turn left into the front yard, so the inside stays private and calm.
china/beijing-capital.c75b9a220992: Tian’anmen. On October first, nineteen forty-nine, Chairman Mao Zedong stood on this gate tower and proclaimed the founding of the People’s Republic of China. The square in front can hold about a million people.
china/beijing-capital.8abf13853a92: Built in fourteen nineteen. Its gate tower is about forty-three meters tall, or one hundred forty-one feet. It’s the tallest of old Beijing’s city gates.
china/beijing-capital.c28493b2176f: The Forbidden City, Palace Museum. Home of twenty-four Ming and Qing emperors. Built fourteen oh six to fourteen twenty. About nine hundred sixty-one meters long and seven hundred fifty-three meters wide, about seventy-two hectares, about one hundred thirty-five football fields, ringed by a ten-meter wall and a wide moat. About eight thousand seven hundred rooms, counted in 间, the space between four pillars. The Hall of Supreme Harmony on the axis is China’s largest surviving wooden hall. You go in through the Meridian Gate, 午门, in the south and out through the Gate of Divine Prowess, 神武门, in the north. It became the Palace Museum in nineteen twenty-five and a World Heritage Site in nineteen eighty-seven.
china/beijing-capital.097cb645600e: Zhengyangmen, Qianmen. Main south gate of the inner city. Built in fourteen nineteen. Its gate tower is about forty-three meters tall, or one hundred forty-one feet, the tallest of old Beijing’s city gates. In front stands an arrow tower with rows of small windows, built for archers to defend the gate. Outside it, Qianmen Street has been a busy shopping street for centuries.
china/beijing-capital.9eb1fa8f6ad9: Why would a city of more than twenty million people be built around one perfectly straight line? This line is seven point eight kilometers long, runs right through the emperor’s throne, and has been Beijing’s backbone for more than seven hundred years. That length is about four point eight miles. In twenty twenty-four it became a World Heritage Site.
china/beijing-capital.6d6e4737f2e7: Question one of twelve. Most hutongs in old Beijing run east-west so that
china/beijing-capital.9b964a782e1f: Built in fourteen seventeen as the front gate of the Imperial City, and given the name Tian’anmen in sixteen fifty-one.
china/beijing-capital.afebdd5fa7a9: Main hall, 正房. North side, facing south. The biggest, tallest building, for the grandparents or the head of the family. It faces south, so the low winter sun shines deep inside, while its wide eaves block the high summer sun. Its solid back wall faces north, into the cold winter wind.
china/beijing-capital.ca295a6fef4c: A siheyuan, 四合院, is a traditional Beijing home: four buildings around a courtyard. The lanes between rows of them are hutongs, 胡同. Change the season, the time of day and the way the house faces, and watch how sunlight reaches the main hall. Your question: why did old Beijing put the main hall facing south?
china/beijing-capital.320c18ab04e4: Temple of Heaven. Where emperors prayed for good harvests. Built in fourteen twenty for the Ming and Qing emperors to worship heaven and pray for good harvests. World Heritage Site since nineteen ninety-eight. The round Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests has three blue roofs: blue for the sky. It is about thirty-eight meters tall, or one hundred twenty-five feet. The park wall is round in the north and square in the south: “round heaven, square earth”, 天圆地方.
china/beijing-capital.79a6792dba9a: about fifteen miles. The Capital Beltway around Washington, D.C. is about sixty-four miles, one hundred three kilometers.
china/beijing-capital.16b9e5b73f32: In July twenty twenty-four, “Beijing Central Axis: A Building Ensemble Exhibiting the Ideal Order of the Chinese Capital” joined the World Heritage List as China’s fifty-ninth World Heritage Site. It has fifteen parts, including the Bell and Drum Towers, Wanning Bridge, Jingshan, the Forbidden City, Tian’anmen, the buildings of Tian’anmen Square, Zhengyangmen, the Temple of Heaven, the Xiannongtan altar and Yongdingmen.
china/beijing-capital.fc3666489c23: Side rooms, 耳房. Small rooms beside the main hall. Lower and smaller, like “ears” on either side of the main hall. Used for storage, a kitchen or a study.
china/beijing-capital.187d5fc74ce9: The round Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests has three blue roofs: blue for the sky. It is about thirty-eight meters tall, or one hundred twenty-five feet.
china/beijing-capital.2138e949e107: Torn down in nineteen fifty-seven to make room for traffic, then rebuilt in two thousand four from old drawings and photos.
china/beijing-capital.146b93d1d0d6: Jingshan. A man-made hill with the best view. Piled up in the Ming dynasty, largely from the earth dug out for the palace moat. About forty-five meters high, or one hundred fifty feet. The Wanchun Pavilion on top sits exactly on the axis. From the top you can see the golden roofs of the Forbidden City to the south and the Drum Tower to the north.
china/beijing-capital.ce00426dbb32: Today the line extends north to the Olympic Green, where the two thousand eight “Bird’s Nest” stadium and “Water Cube” stand on either side of it, and south toward Beijing Daxing International Airport, opened in twenty nineteen.
china/beijing-capital.a64020f0294f: Monument to the People’s Heroes. Today: Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. A thirty-eight-meter granite obelisk on the Central Axis, honouring the people who gave their lives for China’s independence and liberation.
china/beijing-capital.d551a8e02b92: Xiannongtan, Altar of Agriculture. West of the axis. Built in fourteen twenty. Each spring the emperor came here to plough a small field himself, to show how important farming was. It sits to the west of the axis, balancing the Temple of Heaven to the east. Today it houses the Beijing Ancient Architecture Museum.
china/beijing-capital.63ebca0431da: Drum Tower. Telling the time at night. First built in twelve seventy-two, Yuan, rebuilt in the Ming dynasty. About forty-seven meters tall, or one hundred fifty-four feet. Drums were beaten to mark the hours of the night: “morning bell, evening drum”, 晨钟暮鼓. It once held twenty-five drums: one huge drum and twenty-four smaller ones, one for each of the twenty-four solar terms.
china/beijing-capital.8a7048348c0e: Built in fourteen twenty. Each spring the emperor came here to plough a small field himself, to show how important farming was.
china/beijing-capital.c4afd6a78a04: about eighteen miles. The Capital Beltway around Washington, D.C. is about sixty-four miles, one hundred three kilometers.
china/beijing-capital.07f90c28c0d2: Mission one, Walk from Yongdingmen to the Bell Tower
china/beijing-capital.6456112bff63: About forty-four hectares: roughly eighty US football fields.
china/beijing-capital.dcff64a1131c: Summer Palace. Today: Haidian, Beijing. A huge royal garden with Longevity Hill and Kunming Lake. Its Long Corridor is painted with more than fourteen thousand pictures.
china/beijing-capital.7bf47835757b: West wing, 西厢房. Faces east. More bedrooms for the younger generation. It gets the morning sun.
china/beijing-capital.d9a3f9e97b28: Courtyard, 院子. The family’s outdoor living room. All the rooms open onto the yard, not onto the street: quiet, safe and sunny. Families planted trees such as jujube and crabapple, raised goldfish and sat out on summer evenings.
china/beijing-capital.c04551375674: South row, 倒座房. Faces north, toward the yard. Its back wall is on the hutong, and its windows face north into the front yard. It gets the least sun, so it was used for guests, servants, storage or a study.
china/beijing-capital.aaadd6f7454e: On the first of October, nineteen forty-nine, the founding ceremony of the People’s Republic of China was held here.
china/beijing-capital.72f74863cb15: Olympic Park. The “Bird’s Nest” stadium and the “Water Cube” stand on either side of the Central Axis. Beijing is the first city to host both Summer and Winter Olympics, the Summer Olympics in two thousand eight and the Winter Olympics in twenty twenty-two.
china/beijing-capital.3c4a6abd57d3: Great Hall of the People. Today: West side of Tian’anmen Square, Beijing. The National People’s Congress meets here. Its main auditorium seats about ten thousand people.
china/beijing-capital.832efe8f48bd: Mission two, Design a courtyard house that’s warm in winter
china/beijing-capital.55ec19dfc0bf: Drum Tower and Bell Tower. Drums sounded the hours at night and the bell rang at dawn. The bronze bell in the Bell Tower weighs about sixty-three tonnes.
china/beijing-capital.4b5489100ce0: Beyond the textbook, for reference: the dates, heights and distances of the axis buildings; ring road lengths and completion years, second about thirty-two point seven kilometers, nineteen ninety-two; third about forty-eight kilometers, nineteen ninety-four; fourth about sixty-five kilometers, two thousand one; fifth about ninety-eight kilometers, two thousand three; sixth about one hundred eighty-eight kilometers, two thousand nine; the city-growth map is schematic; the courtyard sunlight uses latitude thirty-nine point nine degrees north and a simplified zero point nine meter eave overhang;
china/beijing-capital.bfaa65057247: Mission three, One day on the Central Axis
china/beijing-capital.1c0e74c1b95e: Suggested flow: one, walk the axis in Mission one and have students name the symmetric pairs, “temple left, altar right”; two, use the city slider to compare Yuan Dadu, today: Beijing, Ming-Qing Beijing and the ring roads; three, in the courtyard mission, explain “sitting north, facing south” with the noon sun height at the winter and summer solstices, then link it to the winter monsoon;
china/beijing-capital.77172be2216e: Bell Tower. The northern end of the axis. Rebuilt in seventeen forty-five to seventeen forty-seven during the Qing dynasty, entirely of brick and stone, so it could not burn down again. About forty-eight meters tall, or one hundred fifty-seven feet. Its bronze bell, cast in the Ming Yongle years, weighs about sixty-three tonnes: as much as five school buses. You have walked about seven point eight kilometers, about four point eight miles!
china/beijing-capital.d4d447251a37: On the axis: the Monument to the People’s Heroes, completed nineteen fifty-eight. On the sides: the Great Hall of the People, west, where the National People’s Congress meets, and the National Museum of China, east.
china/beijing-capital.dea48e02542c: Tian’anmen Square. One of the largest city squares in the world. About forty-four hectares: roughly eighty US football fields. A national flag-raising ceremony is held here at sunrise every day. On the axis: the Monument to the People’s Heroes, completed nineteen fifty-eight. On the sides: the Great Hall of the People, west, where the National People’s Congress meets, and the National Museum of China, east.
china/beijing-capital.80e815e33ea3: Zhengyangmen, Qianmen. At about forty-three meters, it was the tallest gate of old Beijing. In front stands an arrow tower with rows of little windows for archers.
china/beijing-capital.a45d82522dc4: From here the axis runs dead straight north for about seven point eight kilometers, four point eight miles.
china/beijing-capital.278b38aaef10: Hutong, 胡同. The lane outside. Old Beijing’s lanes. Most of them run east-west, so the courtyard houses between them can all face south. Many hutongs date back to the Yuan dynasty; one popular theory says the word comes from a Mongolian word for “well”.
china/beijing-capital.fabe804627f0: Click at least four different parts of the house.
china/beijing-capital.724f309b342b: The Beijing Central Axis, 北京中轴线, runs from Yongdingmen Gate in the south to the Drum and Bell Towers in the north: about seven point eight kilometers. Drag the slider below, or press, to walk north. Each time you pass a landmark, its card pops up on the right.
china/beijing-capital.76e228fe5ae7: The National Mall runs west from the Capitol past the Washington Monument to the Lincoln Memorial: about three point two kilometers, two miles, also a planned city axis. Beijing’s Central Axis is about two point four times as long, and more than five hundred years older.
china/beijing-capital.009266573f22: Yongdingmen Gate. The southern start of the axis. Built in fifteen fifty-three, Ming dynasty, as the main south gate of the new outer city. The name means “Gate of Lasting Peace”. Torn down in nineteen fifty-seven to make room for traffic, then rebuilt in two thousand four from old drawings and photos. From here the axis runs dead straight north for about seven point eight kilometers, four point eight miles.
china/beijing-capital.c8b949c2fa30: Note: the three D model is schematic. Buildings are enlarged, and positions and distances are approximate.

china/china-space.2a08955a980c: Memory hook: Five carried one: Shenzhou five, Yang Liwei, two thousand three.
china/china-space.ef385bc75d9b: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou one was uncrewed. The first crewed Shenzhou was number five.
china/china-space.4493c51167ac: Don’t mix up: Chang’e three landed on the near side, which faces Earth. The far side came next, with Chang’e four.
china/china-space.6214bbf54933: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five did not carry astronauts. Robots collected the samples.
china/china-space.53914f91f44b: Twenty twenty-two. The Tiangong space station is complete. Three modules — Tianhe in twenty twenty-one, Wentian in July twenty twenty-two, and Mengtian in October twenty twenty-two — joined in a T shape about four hundred kilometers up, or two hundred fifty miles up. In November twenty twenty-two two crews, six astronauts, met in orbit for the first time.
china/china-space.48a98526f50f: Don’t mix up: Dongfanghong one carried no people. China’s first astronaut flew thirty-three years later, in two thousand three.
china/china-space.d4bb3a4629aa: Memory hook: Orbit, land, return — 绕, 落, 回.
china/china-space.eb332f206bb2: Two thousand three. Shenzhou five: Yang Liwei, China’s first astronaut. Yang Liwei, 杨利伟, circled Earth fourteen times in about twenty-one hours. China became the third country — after the USSR and the USA — to send a person into space on its own rocket.
china/china-space.8198af0d5622: Twenty thirteen. Chang’e three lands; the Yutu rover rolls off. Chang’e three made the first soft landing on the Moon by any country since nineteen seventy-six, in the Bay of Rainbows region on the near side. It released Yutu, 玉兔, the “Jade Rabbit” who lives with Chang’e in the legend.
china/china-space.3d213d293d16: Twenty twenty-five. Tianwen two heads for an asteroid. On the twenty-ninth of May, twenty twenty-five, a Long March three B launched Tianwen two to collect samples from a small near-Earth asteroid, Kamoʻoalewa. That year China launched about ninety-two rockets — a record. Next goal: Chinese astronauts on the Moon before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.f425f2b535ab: Two thousand seven. Chang’e one orbits the Moon. The lunar programme is named after Chang’e, 嫦娥, the Moon goddess of Chinese legend. Its plan has three steps: orbit, 绕, land, 落, return, 回. Chang’e one did step one and mapped the whole Moon.
china/china-space.d932f0b5989f: Nineteen ninety-nine. Shenzhou one: a test flight with no crew. China’s crewed spaceflight programme, started in nineteen ninety-two, flew its first spacecraft. Shenzhou, 神舟, means “divine vessel”. Four uncrewed test flights came before anyone climbed aboard.
china/china-space.0408752007b4: Twenty twenty. Chang’e five brings the Moon home. The giant Long March five sent Chang’e five from Wenchang on Hainan Island. It landed in the Ocean of Storms, drilled and scooped one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams of rock and soil, or three point eight pounds, launched back into lunar orbit, and returned to Earth on the seventeenth of December — completing “orbit, land, return”.
china/china-space.fea499163320: Twenty twenty-one. Tianwen one lands the Zhurong rover on Mars. Tianwen one, 天问, “Questions to Heaven”, after an ancient poem, did three jobs on its first try: orbit Mars, land, and drive a rover. Zhurong, 祝融, is named after the god of fire. China became the second country to drive a rover on Mars, after the USA.
china/china-space.99a424c71a94: Don’t mix up: Chang’e is a robot programme. No Chinese astronaut has walked on the Moon yet; that goal is set for before twenty thirty.
china/china-space.8330be9dbfb8: Nineteen seventy. Dongfanghong one: China’s first satellite. A Long March one rocket lifted the one hundred seventy-three kilogram satellite — about three hundred eighty pounds — from Jiuquan in the Gobi Desert. From orbit it played the song “The East Is Red”, 东方红, back to Earth. China became the fifth country to launch its own satellite.
china/china-space.83467910a458: Memory hook: Five went and came back: one thousand seven hundred thirty-one grams.
china/china-space.190327abf1bc: Twenty twelve. Shenzhou nine: the first hand-flown docking. In twenty eleven China launched a small space lab, Tiangong one, 天宫, “Heavenly Palace”, and the uncrewed Shenzhou eight docked with it automatically. In June twenty twelve astronaut Liu Wang flew Shenzhou nine in by hand. On board was Liu Yang, China’s first woman in space.
china/china-space.3547a4e0d288: Two thousand eight. Shenzhou seven: China’s first spacewalk. Zhai Zhigang, 翟志刚, opened the hatch and stepped out into space, waving a Chinese flag. He wore a spacesuit made in China called Feitian, 飞天, “flying to the heavens”.
china/china-space.8f61a3f30cde: Twenty twenty-four. Chang’e six: samples from the far side. Relaying through the new Queqiao two satellite, Chang’e six landed in Apollo crater on the far side, collected one thousand nine hundred thirty-five point three grams of samples, and came home on the twenty-fifth of June — the first far-side samples in history.
china/china-space.03d9176a2850: Don’t mix up: Tiangong one was a small test lab, not the big Tiangong space station of twenty twenty-two.
china/china-space.b63fe82444b7: Don’t mix up: Chang’e five samples are from the near side; Chang’e six samples are from the far side.
china/china-space.06248eb0c510: Don’t mix up: Shenzhou seven was the spacewalk mission; docking came later, with Shenzhou eight and nine.
china/china-space.2696e6ede982: Twenty nineteen. Chang’e four: first-ever landing on the far side. Nobody had ever landed on the far side, because you can’t radio Earth from there. First China parked the Queqiao relay satellite beyond the Moon, May twenty eighteen. Then Chang’e four landed in Von Kármán crater and sent out the Yutu two rover.
china/china-space.8b538725ab3e: Memory hook: Nineteen seventy: the East is Red — and so is the sky.
china/china-space.88d193c46b0e: Don’t mix up: Third country to fly people into space — not the first. And Shenzhou five did not go to the Moon.

china/chinese-spirit.fc8d12da6fa9: Nineteen sixty-four. Yuan Longping. Yuan finds a male-sterile rice plant.
china/chinese-spirit.a6b8c360e1a0: Nineteen seventy-one. Tu Youyou. A sweet wormwood extract works against malaria parasites in an animal test.
china/chinese-spirit.0be52e54e541: Nineteen seventy-two. Tu Youyou. Tu’s team isolates the compound later named artemisinin.
china/chinese-spirit.04cda3fb6982: Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu grew up in China and worked as a physicist in the U.S. She and her collaborators showed that one kind of radioactive decay behaves differently from its mirror image. They cooled cobalt sixty and used a magnetic field to line up its nuclear spins. More electrons came out in the direction opposite to the spins.
china/chinese-spirit.5bc875302d28: Tu Youyou. Tu led a team that discovered artemisinin, a compound used to treat malaria. She received half of the twenty fifteen Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. A fourth-century medical text by Ge Hong described soaking sweet wormwood. That gave Tu’s team an idea: try extracting substances from the plant at a lower temperature.
china/chinese-spirit.ee8dd4c61dfe: Nineteen fifty-seven. Chien-Shiung Wu. Wu and her collaborators publish their experimental results.
china/chinese-spirit.8ad0a6d139cf: Nineteen sixty. Red Flag Canal workers. Work begins on the Red Flag Canal in Lin County.
china/chinese-spirit.47a11bab4e6c: Yuan Longping. Yuan and other researchers bred high-yield hybrid rice by crossing different lines of rice. In nineteen sixty-four, he examined clusters of rice flowers with a magnifying glass. He found a male-sterile plant. It made no pollen that could fertilize an egg, but pollen from another line could help it set seed.
china/chinese-spirit.42a15f79dc54: Twenty fifteen. Tu Youyou. Tu shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
china/chinese-spirit.e5e7ac5e05f5: Nineteen sixty-nine. Red Flag Canal workers. The full Red Flag Canal network, including its branch channels, is completed.
china/chinese-spirit.e2781c3bcfc1: Qian Xuesen. Qian worked with Caltech’s early rocketry team and later helped build China’s rocket and space programs. U.S. authorities barred him from leaving for several years. Once the ban was lifted in nineteen fifty-five, he and his family left Los Angeles by ship for China.
china/chinese-spirit.c023bfa65609: Nineteen sixty-five. Red Flag Canal workers. Water begins flowing through the Red Flag Canal’s main channel.
china/chinese-spirit.24348324c1f5: Zhan Tianyou. Zhan led construction of the railway from Beijing to Zhangjiakou. It opened in nineteen oh nine. At Qinglongqiao, he laid out a switchback. Trains could take a longer route up the mountain by reversing direction on the tracks.
china/chinese-spirit.ca51d520fca2: Nineteen fifty-eight. Deng Jiaxian. Deng takes on classified research.
china/chinese-spirit.1440f9ef8e5d: Deng Jiaxian. Deng led teams in China’s early nuclear weapons program. Yang Zhenning later wrote about him in the essay “Deng Jiaxian.” In nineteen fifty-eight he took on classified work. He could no longer tell even his family where he was going for work.
china/chinese-spirit.456036058abb: Nineteen fifty-five. Qian Xuesen. After the U.S. travel ban is lifted, Qian returns to China.
china/chinese-spirit.acf377ba63a7: Nineteen thirty. Wen Yiduo. Wen takes a teaching post in Qingdao, where he studies Tang poetry.
china/chinese-spirit.6215996c0488: Nineteen oh nine. Zhan Tianyou. The Beijing-Zhangjiakou Railway opens.
china/chinese-spirit.4a6729b7aa12: Nineteen twenty-nine. Lin Qiaozhi. Lin graduates and joins the staff at Peking Union Medical College Hospital.
china/chinese-spirit.fceafdeabd25: Lin Qiaozhi. Lin cared for mothers and newborns and helped develop medical care for women in China. In the nineteen fifties, she sent staff to the Soviet Union to learn how to examine cells for signs of disease. After they returned, her team began screening for cervical cancer.

china/disasters.9196b34b47c0: Ürümqi. The city farthest from any ocean in the world — about two thousand five hundred kilometers.
china/disasters.caa32b65bf70: Three-North Shelter Forest. Today: Northwest, North and Northeast China. The “Great Green Wall”: belts of trees planted across northern China since nineteen seventy-eight to hold back wind and sand.
china/disasters.e0b6a3656b75: Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. The highest plateau on Earth, on average over four thousand meters. The Yangtze, Yellow and Lancang, Mekong, rivers all start here.
china/disasters.50d579a0e204: Hainan Island. China’s second-largest island, warm all year round. It became a province and the biggest Special Economic Zone in nineteen eighty-eight.
china/disasters.e9ab009d79ef: Wenchuan. Today: Wenchuan County, Aba, Sichuan. The most destructive earthquake since nineteen forty-nine. Rescuers came from all over China, and every province helped rebuild a stricken county with stronger schools and homes.
china/disasters.19f7504a3925: Longmen Shan. Today: Western edge of the Sichuan Basin. Where the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau pushes east against the Sichuan Basin. The rocks along this fault snapped in two thousand eight and caused the Wenchuan earthquake.

china/division-integration.3bc7f634e352: Chang’an, Xi’an, Sui capital. Capital of the Sui. In five eighty-one Yang Jian founded the Sui with Chang’an as capital. In five eighty-nine the Sui conquered the Chen dynasty and reunified China.
china/division-integration.eddc2902cad0: In three hundred seventeen Sima Rui founded the Eastern Jin at Jiankang, while the north entered the Sixteen Kingdoms period. Large numbers of northerners moved south, bringing labour and advanced farming techniques; with good natural conditions and relative peace, the Jiangnan region was developed.
china/division-integration.f353e0e234d2: Northern Wei later split into Eastern and Western Wei, replaced by Northern Qi and Northern Zhou. In five hundred eighty-one Yang Jian founded the Sui; in five hundred eighty-nine Sui conquered Chen and reunified north and south, ending nearly four centuries of division.
china/division-integration.003500dc809f: Late in the Eastern Han, the Yellow Turban uprising broke out in one hundred eighty-four. Afterwards local strongmen and officials raised their own armies: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao in the north, the Sun family in Jiangdong, Liu Biao in Jing Province and Liu Zhang in Yi Province.
china/division-integration.a7e07067109e: Battle of Chibi, two hundred eight. Around today’s Chibi, Hubei, Sun Quan and Liu Bei versus Cao Cao. In two hundred eight Cao Cao marched south; the allied armies of Sun Quan and Liu Bei attacked his fleet with fire at Chibi on the Yangtze. Cao Cao retreated north; this laid the foundation for the three kingdoms.
china/division-integration.c215abd53f1d: Pingcheng, Datong. Early capital of Northern Wei. Northern Wei’s capital before four ninety-four. Emperor Xiaowen left it for Luoyang, closer to the Central Plains, to rule the north and learn from Han culture. The Yungang Grottoes were carved near Pingcheng.
china/division-integration.de413b617127: Yizhou, Taiwan. Reached by Wu’s fleet in two hundred thirty. In two hundred thirty Sun Quan sent Wei Wen with over ten thousand men by sea to Yizhou. It strengthened the links between the mainland and Taiwan.
china/division-integration.3e37786e144c: Battle of the Fei River, three eighty-three. Around today’s Shou County, Anhui, Eastern Jin versus Former Qin. Former Qin, which had unified the north, attacked the Eastern Jin with a huge army. The Eastern Jin won with far fewer troops; the idioms “every bush and tree looks like an enemy soldier” come from this battle.
china/division-integration.d45df3995189: The Northern Wei, founded by the Tuoba branch of the Xianbei, unified the Yellow River valley in four hundred thirty-nine. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang and carried out reforms to adopt Han culture, promoting the blending of the northern peoples.
china/division-integration.04cf07081065: Each kingdom developed: Wei built irrigation and military farms, and the northern economy recovered; Zhuge Liang governed Shu and developed the southwest; in two hundred thirty Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou, today’s Taiwan, strengthening links between the mainland and Taiwan.
china/division-integration.fab5688d590a: In three hundred eighty-three, at the Battle of the Fei River, the Eastern Jin defeated Former Qin, which had unified the north, with far fewer troops. From four hundred twenty the south was ruled in turn by the Song, Qi, Liang and Chen — the Southern Dynasties — all from Jiankang.
china/division-integration.b5f1d0f40a74: Battle of the Fei River, three hundred eighty-three
china/division-integration.1b054a5850bc: Wei. In two hundred twenty Cao Pi became emperor; capital Luoyang. Wei built irrigation works and military farms, tuntian; the northern economy recovered. Wei conquered Shu in two hundred sixty-three.
china/division-integration.73b83d0637cf: Shu, Han. In two hundred twenty-one Liu Bei became emperor in Chengdu; the state is called Shu. Zhuge Liang governed well and helped develop the southwest.
china/division-integration.ad734287abba: In two hundred Cao Cao met Yuan Shao at Guandu. Though outnumbered, Cao Cao raided Wuchao and burned Yuan’s grain — a victory of the few over the many. Afterwards Cao Cao gradually unified the north.
china/division-integration.b880c5b9d7cc: Sui. In five eighty-one Yang Jian founded the Sui; in five eighty-nine Sui conquered Chen and reunified north and south. Nearly four centuries of division came to an end.
china/division-integration.1cc6070a3dcc: Wei conquered Shu in two hundred sixty-three; in two hundred sixty-six Sima Yan founded the Western Jin at Luoyang, and in two hundred eighty it conquered Wu, ending the division. Meanwhile the Xiongnu, Xianbei, Jie, Di and Qiang moved inward in large numbers and lived among the Han. After the War of the Eight Princes, the Western Jin fell in three hundred sixteen.
china/division-integration.ac192b64d3b7: Luoyang. Capital of Wei, Western Jin and Northern Wei, the last after four ninety-four. Cao Pi made Luoyang the capital of Wei in two twenty; the Western Jin kept it. In four ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen moved the Northern Wei capital here from Pingcheng.
china/division-integration.57c3f34cda18: Jianye or Jiankang, Nanjing. Capital of Wu, Eastern Jin and the Southern Dynasties. Wu’s capital Jianye was renamed Jiankang in the Jin. Eastern Jin and all four Southern Dynasties, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, ruled from here; it became a great commercial city.
china/division-integration.31f3f69f2281: Battle of Guandu, two hundred. Near today’s Zhongmou, Henan, Cao Cao versus Yuan Shao. Cao Cao, with a smaller army, burned Yuan Shao’s grain stores at Wuchao and won. A famous victory of the few over the many; it laid the foundation for Cao Cao to unify the north.
china/division-integration.456e999e022f: Common mix-up: Guandu unified the north in two hundred; Chibi laid the foundation of the three kingdoms in two oh eight. Don’t swap them.

china/dynasties.06c1bc5caede: In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen of Northern Wei, a Xianbei 鲜卑 ruler, moved his capital to Luoyang and had his court adopt Han clothes, language and surnames — a big step in the blending of peoples.
china/dynasties.d60c3e2d3a2f: Memory hook Dynasty Song: 夏商与西周, 东周分两段;
china/dynasties.7fc59db76aac: Shang. Circa sixteen hundred to ten forty-six B C E. Pan Geng moves the capital to Yin. Around thirteen hundred B C E King Pan Geng moved the capital to Yin. Shang settled down there for the rest of the dynasty — and Yin’s ruins, 殷墟, later gave up thousands of oracle bones. Shang kings asked their ancestors questions by cracking turtle shells and ox bones. The answers were carved on them: oracle-bone script, 甲骨文, the oldest mature Chinese writing. The Houmuwu ding, 后母戊鼎, weighs eight hundred thirty-two point eight four kilograms, one thousand eight hundred thirty-six pounds — more than a grand piano. It is the heaviest ancient bronze vessel found in China.
china/dynasties.c2ebc1257f5e: Qing. Sixteen forty-four to nineteen twelve, name Qing from sixteen thirty-six. Kangxi: Taiwan and the Russian border. In sixteen eighty-three Qing brought Taiwan under its rule and in sixteen eighty-four set up Taiwan Prefecture. In sixteen eighty-nine the Treaty of Nerchinsk, 尼布楚条约, with Russia set the northeast border. Emperor Qianlong put down revolts in Xinjiang in the seventeen fifties and secured Qing rule there. Eighteen forty: the Opium War — the start of modern Chinese history. Nineteen twelve: the last emperor abdicated.
china/dynasties.6c225ac12e4f: The USA is about two hundred fifty years old. China’s Tang dynasty alone lasted two hundred ninety years — and from the first dynasty to the last is almost four thousand years. Could you put them all in order?
china/dynasties.4e412e915e7b: Five hundred eighty-nine: Sui conquered Chen and reunited China after almost three hundred years of division.
china/dynasties.acf515a29dd6: Jin conquered Wu in two hundred eighty and ended sixty years of division. It lasted about thirty-five years before the north broke apart again.
china/dynasties.d8afe1f61bc3: Kublai Khan named his dynasty Yuan in twelve seventy-one. Yuan took Lin’an, today: Hangzhou, in twelve seventy-six and finished off the last Song resistance in twelve seventy-nine.
china/dynasties.a2b969f2e59a: Shang kings asked their ancestors questions by cracking turtle shells and ox bones. The answers were carved on them: oracle-bone script, 甲骨文, the oldest mature Chinese writing.
china/dynasties.0044fc94c27d: Round one: drag the dynasty cards into the right order, or tap one card, then another, to swap them, and press Check — every check with mistakes adds a five-second penalty. Round two: match capitals, people and inventions to their dynasty, plus five seconds per wrong answer. Your total time decides your rank in the imperial exam!
china/dynasties.c073ff54129d: “When Suzhou and Huzhou have a good harvest, the whole country has enough”, 苏湖熟, 天下足.
china/dynasties.cdc64cf75b64: Zhang Heng, 张衡, built a seismoscope, 地动仪, that showed the direction of distant earthquakes.
china/dynasties.991fb41152a4: Pingcheng. Today: Datong, Shanxi. The Northern Wei ruled the north from Pingcheng. In four hundred ninety-four Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital south to Luoyang to be closer to the Central Plains.
china/dynasties.f55657dbe78a: Drag the year, twenty seventy B C E to nineteen twelve C E, or press “Next dynasty”. The territory morphs, the star marks the capital, and the card tells you each era’s big moment. Visit all nineteen eras to finish the mission.
china/dynasties.980ac8838213: In two hundred sixty-six Sima Yan took the throne from Wei and founded Jin.
china/dynasties.e7df7fe8aae9: Don’t mix up: Qing didn’t start in sixteen forty-four: Hong Taiji renamed his state Qing in sixteen thirty-six; in sixteen forty-four Qing armies entered Beijing.

china/early-civilization.4fea711629dd: In Yuanmou, Yunnan, scientists found early humans from about one point seven million years ago: Yuanmou Man, the earliest early humans so far confirmed in China.
china/early-civilization.3ed13b3215e5: About four thousand to five thousand years ago, the Yan and Yellow Emperor tribes of the Yellow River valley allied, defeated Chiyou at Zhuolu, and gradually formed the Huaxia people. The two are honoured as the first ancestors of Chinese civilization.
china/early-civilization.ae08a11f0834: At Zhoukoudian near Beijing lived Peking Man, about seven hundred thousand to two hundred thousand years ago. They made chipped stone tools, used natural fire and lived in groups.
china/early-civilization.39dbb016706d: Zoom in on the last few thousand years: Hemudu, Banpo, the legendary age of the Yan and Yellow Emperors, then Yao, Shun and Yu, about twenty seventy B C E, Yu founds the Xia dynasty.
china/early-civilization.9b86dc8d89a2: In a cave at the top of the same hill lived Upper Cave Man, about thirty thousand years ago. They looked like modern people and sewed clothes with bone needles.
china/early-civilization.4d1340515429: Farming began about ten thousand years ago. Along the Yangtze, Hemudu people grew RICE, about seven thousand years ago; along the Yellow River, Banpo people grew MILLET, about six thousand years ago.

china/great-wall.d50c346e1c9b: Rammed earth, 夯土, is damp soil poured between wooden boards and pounded hard, one layer of about ten to twenty centimeters at a time, or four to eight inches per layer. Pounded earth gets rock-hard — in the dry northwest, Han walls built this way still stand after two thousand years.
china/great-wall.d61e8b38cd3d: After driving the Mongols north, Ming spent about two centuries building the brick-and-stone wall most visitors see today — from Hushan on the Yalu River to Jiayu Pass: eight thousand eight hundred fifty-one point eight kilometers including natural barriers, two thousand nine survey.
china/great-wall.3ab4b5806ea8: The inner side usually has a lower wall, 宇墙, so soldiers don’t fall off.
china/great-wall.77949e590c0f: Guarding the road to Juyong Pass and Beijing. On average the wall here is about seven point eight meters high and five point eight meters wide on top, or twenty-six feet high and nineteen feet wide — five horses side by side. It’s the most-visited section.
china/great-wall.e7b58cf331f1: Curriculum: Grade seven Book one, Unit three, Qin unification — Meng Tian drives back the Xiongnu; the wall from Lintao, today: Min County, Gansu, to Liaodong, and Book two, Unit three, the Ming wall from the Yalu River to Jiayu Pass; Qi Jiguang.
china/great-wall.9700a799bf74: Smoke by day, fire by night, 白天放烟, 夜间举火: tower to tower, the alarm raced to the rear.
china/great-wall.8d21a82496ff: The real thing. The Mutianyu section of the Great Wall, Beijing — watchtowers one after another along the ridge.
china/great-wall.d7199941020d: The walkway on top. A road for soldiers along the mountains. At Badaling the top is about five point eight meters wide, or nineteen feet — room for five horses or ten soldiers side by side. Soldiers could move quickly along the wall to wherever the attack came.
china/great-wall.d13ac81d5685: Hollow watchtower, 空心敌台. A fort astride the wall. General Qi Jiguang, 戚继光, famous for fighting pirates, had over a thousand hollow towers built on the wall near Beijing. Soldiers lived and stored weapons inside, and shot along the wall from the windows — crossfire against ladders.
china/great-wall.f08e02021348: The wall is about six meters wide, or twenty feet — nineteen times too narrow for your eye. And it’s the same colour as the hills around it.
china/great-wall.c4f314d4c86f: Qinhuangdao, Hebei, built thirteen eighty-one, Ming
china/great-wall.212cb1e37732: Question one of twelve. The Great Wall became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in…
china/great-wall.f8c0fef08070: Mission one: build a wall — then hold the pass
china/great-wall.a87f75966b68: Sources: China’s State Administration of Cultural Heritage, twenty twelve survey, walls and trenches of all dynasties: twenty-one thousand one hundred ninety-six point one eight kilometers; two thousand nine Ming wall survey with the national mapping agency, eight thousand eight hundred fifty-one point eight kilometers equals six thousand two hundred fifty-nine point six kilometers of built wall plus three hundred fifty-nine point seven kilometers of trenches plus two thousand two hundred thirty-two point five kilometers of natural barriers such as cliffs and rivers. Comparison distances are approximate.
china/great-wall.982add46bf00: Shanhai Pass, 山海关. “The First Pass Under Heaven”, 天下第一关, where mountains, 山, meet the sea, 海. At Old Dragon’s Head the wall runs right into the Bohai Sea. In sixteen forty-four Qing armies entered the central plains through this pass.
china/great-wall.63bd023fa4f1: The western end of the Ming wall: a fort in the narrow gap between the Qilian Mountains and the Hei Mountains, on the Silk Road. Nicknamed “the mightiest pass under heaven”, 天下第一雄关.
china/great-wall.a7b485a9e130: The real thing. The Ming wall at Badaling, north-west of Beijing.
china/great-wall.4fb68aad4546: The wall, about six meters or twenty feet wide, is wider than that — from a plane you can spot it.
china/great-wall.3219aa5544b2: Yumen Pass, 玉门关, Dunhuang. A Han gateway to the Western Regions. A Tang poem says “the spring wind never crosses Yumen Pass” — it was that remote. Han walls of gravel and reeds still stand nearby.
china/great-wall.20a06da44f6e: The land itself. Builders used mountains as part of the defence. Walls follow ridgelines, so attackers must climb a steep slope before they even reach the wall. In the game a ridge adds two meters of “effective height”. Rivers and cliffs were used too: two thousand two hundred thirty-two point five kilometers of the Ming line are natural barriers, two thousand nine survey.
china/great-wall.7c7a1b46b593: Added beyond the textbook: the two thousand nine, Ming, and twenty twelve, all dynasties, survey figures; Badaling’s dimensions, commonly published; Han gravel-and-reed construction; inscribed Ming bricks; the space myth, eye resolution of about one arcminute is an approximation; Yang Liwei said after his two thousand three flight that he did not see the wall, as reported at the time.
china/great-wall.e2179605ca48: Qin wall. Qin Shi Huang sent general Meng Tian, 蒙恬, north to drive back the Xiongnu, 匈奴, then joined and extended the old Qin, Zhao and Yan walls: from Lintao, today’s Min County, Gansu, in the west to Liaodong, in today’s Liaoning, in the east — the “ten thousand-li Great Wall”.
china/great-wall.18de77a60d4e: In the game a ridge adds two meters of “effective height”.
china/great-wall.cd7068bc48da: Wooden boards make a mould; damp soil is poured in and pounded with heavy rammers, about ten to twenty centimeters per layer, or four to eight inches.
china/great-wall.7f7b36199b1b: Don’t mix up: The Great Wall was not built once by one emperor: many dynasties built, joined and rebuilt it over two thousand plus years.
china/great-wall.f39b0eb6c082: The Great Wall is not just a wall: it is walls, passes, 关隘, watchtowers and beacon towers working together. Click any part of the model to see what it does.
china/great-wall.3dfba02f31a7: Rammed earth, 夯土. Soil pounded hard, layer by layer. Wooden boards make a mould; damp soil is poured in and pounded with heavy rammers, about ten to twenty centimeters per layer, or four to eight inches. Qin and Han walls are mostly rammed earth or piled stone. Even Ming brick walls often have an earth-and-rubble core inside.
china/great-wall.44164b520b2f: Fired-brick shell. Ming walls wear a brick “coat”. Ming kilns fired huge numbers of bricks; a typical wall brick weighs around ten kilograms or more, approximately. Many bricks are stamped with the year and the workshop — an early quality-control system.
china/great-wall.2bd093ebd623: At Badaling the top is about five point eight meters wide, or nineteen feet — room for five horses or ten soldiers side by side.
china/great-wall.bc4bb0a40a5f: Yanqing, Beijing, built fifteen oh five, Ming
china/great-wall.083bc672a235: Pick a style, terrain, material and height, then press “ Build it layer by layer”. Click any part of the three D model to learn about it. Then press “ Hold the pass”: a storm, or sandstorm, a cavalry raid and a ladder assault. Hold all three using eighty labour points or less for three stars.
china/great-wall.47a23aace4a1: The real thing. Old Dragon’s Head, 老龙头, at Shanhai Pass, where the wall runs into the Bohai Sea.
china/great-wall.b57cdf12d24b: Jiayu Pass, 嘉峪关. The western end of the Ming wall: a fort in the narrow gap between the Qilian Mountains and the Hei Mountains, on the Silk Road. Nicknamed “the mightiest pass under heaven”, 天下第一雄关.
china/great-wall.35781c320566: Ming wall at Badaling: on average about seven point eight meters high, or twenty-six feet; six point five meters wide at the base, or twenty-one feet; and five point eight meters across the top, or nineteen feet — commonly published figures. The Han wall is drawn at a typical surviving size — sections vary a lot. Basketball hoop: three point zero five meters, ten feet; school bus: about three point two meters tall, or ten point five feet.
china/great-wall.055aa08fe7f7: Crenellations, 垛口. Cover for defenders on the outer side. The outer parapet has tall teeth, merlons, with gaps, crenels, to shoot through, plus small holes to look and shoot down. The inner side usually has a lower wall, 宇墙, so soldiers don’t fall off.
china/great-wall.87d656090179: Hushan, 虎山, Dandong. On the Yalu River at the border with North Korea — the eastern starting point of the Ming wall according to the two thousand nine survey.
china/great-wall.da3e41683c74: The numbers in the “hold the pass” and beacon games, labour points, three minutes per hop, eight twelfths of a kilometer visibility, are simplified game values, not historical data. Wall routes on the map are schematic.
china/great-wall.cd26e752c0cd: Mission four: can you see it from space?
china/great-wall.60deb0d8f186: The real thing. The western gate of the Jiayu Pass fort, Gansu — the west end of the Ming wall.
china/great-wall.7c9258210905: Press “ Hold the pass” on the three D stage to test your design.
china/great-wall.4ed1b0e6ebd6: Is the Great Wall really one wall? Can astronauts see it from space? And how do you stop an army with dirt? Add up the walls of every dynasty and you get twenty-one thousand one hundred ninety-six kilometers, thirteen thousand one hundred seventy-one miles — more than two round trips from New York to Los Angeles.
china/great-wall.3eaf993a7381: Mutianyu, 慕田峪. Watchtowers stand close together on a steep, forested ridge. Parts of the wall have crenellations on both sides, so defenders could fight either way.
china/great-wall.28cd5a3cb3dc: Drainage spouts, 吐水嘴. Keep rainwater out of the wall. Stone gutters stick out from the wall so rain pours away from the wall face instead of soaking in. Water is the Great Wall’s worst enemy — it freezes, cracks and washes out earth.
china/great-wall.687c81bcba33: “The First Pass Under Heaven”, 天下第一关, where mountains, 山, meet the sea, 海. At Old Dragon’s Head the wall runs right into the Bohai Sea. In sixteen forty-four Qing armies entered the central plains through this pass.

china/great-wall.3af8b5beec2c: Memory hook: Board, soil, pound, repeat — that’s 版筑, “board building”.

china/great-wall.84e008cfabf5: Gravel and reed layers. Han builders’ trick in the desert. Near Yumen Pass there is little soil, so Han soldiers alternated gravel with layers of reeds or tamarisk branches. The plant layers bind the gravel. In the dry desert these walls have lasted over two thousand years.
china/great-wall.6b33672cfa2f: Qin Shi Huang sent general Meng Tian, 蒙恬, north to drive back the Xiongnu, 匈奴, then joined and extended the old Qin, Zhao and Yan walls: from Lintao, today’s Min County, Gansu, in the west to Liaodong, in today’s Liaoning, in the east — the “ten-thousand-li Great Wall”.

china/great-wall.731fdcb3cca5: On the Yalu River at the border with North Korea — the eastern starting point of the Ming wall according to the two thousand nine survey.
china/great-wall.8e6e826054df: The real thing. ESA astronaut Alexander Gerst photographed this area from the International Space Station to answer “Can you see the Great Wall from the ISS?” — his answer: next to impossible with the naked eye.
china/great-wall.fd596a70e604: General Qi Jiguang, 戚继光, famous for fighting pirates, had over a thousand hollow towers built on the wall near Beijing.
china/great-wall.e33c2dce8806: Jin border trenches. The Jurchen Jin dug long ditches backed by earth walls, 界壕, “border trenches”, across today’s Inner Mongolia and Heilongjiang — against the rising Mongols.
china/great-wall.ff99185a1b00: Near Yumen Pass, today: northwest of Dunhuang, Han builders stacked a layer of gravel, then a layer of reeds or tamarisk branches, again and again. The reeds work like rebar, holding the gravel together against wind. Use what’s local — 就地取材.

china/great-wall.ed506c05382b: Ming kilns fired huge numbers of bricks; a typical wall brick weighs around ten kilograms or more, approximately.

On average the wall here is about seven point eight meters high and five point eight meters wide on top, or twenty-six feet high and nineteen feet wide — five horses side by side. china/great-wall.3e150b557236: Beacon tower, 烽火台. The ancient “text message”. Smoke by day, fire by night, 白天放烟, 夜间举火: tower to tower, the alarm raced to the rear. Beacon towers often stand on hilltops near or ahead of the wall, where they can see far.

china/great-wall.d4f568df57f3: Hushan. Today: Dandong, Liaoning. On the Yalu River at the border with the DPRK, North Korea. The two thousand nine survey put the eastern start of the Ming Great Wall here.
china/great-wall.e1526bc1d563: Suggested use: one, let students find the cheapest design that still holds, then discuss why Qin and Han used earth and Ming used brick, technology, climate, terrain, money; two, use the year slider to show the wall was not built by one dynasty at one time; three, use the space test to practise checking a claim against evidence.
china/great-wall.f77acd16e87a: Rivers and cliffs were used too: two thousand two hundred thirty-two point five kilometers of the Ming line are natural barriers, two thousand nine survey.
china/great-wall.8fc22eb96ffd: The wall is about six meters wide, or twenty feet — eighteen thousand five hundred seventy-nine times too narrow for your eye. And it’s the same colour as the hills around it.
