math/sampling.5663facf613b: Comparing two groups: plant heights without, A, and with, B, fertilizer, ten random plants each. Mean A equals eleven centimeters, mean B equals fifteen centimeters, and both have a mean absolute deviation, MAD, of one point four centimeters. The centers differ by four centimeters, almost three MADs, so the two piles overlap only a little: the fertilizer really seems to help.
math/sampling.694751fc72ce: Here is a jar of three hundred beads, some of them red. The whole jar is the population. What fraction is red? We could count every bead, but for a real population, every voter in a country, every fish in a lake, that is impossible.
math/sampling.d024f2a19434: Now use bigger samples of eighty beads each. The new pile is much narrower: bigger samples vary less, so a single big sample is more likely to land close to the truth.
math/sampling.16b471ff598b: Worked example: in a random sample of fifty students from a school of six hundred, eighteen named soccer as their favourite sport. Sample proportion: eighteen over fifty equals thirty-six percent. Estimate for the whole school: zero point three six times six hundred equals two hundred sixteen students. It is an estimate, not an exact count.
math/sampling.8886bddc6a05: Repeat it forty times. Each dot is one random sample of twenty beads, placed at its percentage of red. The dots pile up into a hill: most samples land near the middle, but some are far off.
math/sampling.889b22dee633: Reveal the truth: ninety of the three hundred beads are red, exactly thirty percent. Both piles are centered near thirty percent. That is inference: the proportion in a random sample is a fair estimate of the proportion in the population.
math/sampling.d490c19f776d: But beware of bias. These red beads were poured in last and the jar was never shaken, so they sit near the top. Grab the twenty beads on top and seventeen are red: eighty-five percent! When not every bead has an equal chance, the sample is biased, and repeating it never fixes that.
math/sampling.5ffffdf7e8e6: Instead, take a random sample: shake the jar and pull out twenty beads without looking, so every bead has the same chance of being picked. This handful has six red out of twenty, so we estimate p hat equals six over twenty equals thirty percent red.
math/sampling.1d0264806707: Put them back, shake, and draw again. This time nine of twenty are red: forty-five percent. Two random samples, two different answers! This natural wobble from sample to sample is called sampling variability.

math/scale-drawings.67cbead2a2a0: What if we stretch only the width? Now eight divided by four equals two but three divided by three equals one. The house looks squashed, so this is not a scale drawing. Every length must use the same factor.
math/scale-drawings.2386e217775f: Here is a little house drawn on graph paper. Its wall is four squares wide and three squares tall. How can we draw it bigger without changing its shape?
math/scale-drawings.cd63410f892a: Multiply every length by the same number. Here each length doubles: four becomes eight and three becomes six. That number is the scale factor, k equals two.
math/scale-drawings.aa173e87c388: Now area. A three by two rectangle covers six squares. Scale it by k equals two: every square becomes a two by two block of four squares, so the area becomes four times six equals twenty-four, not twelve!
math/scale-drawings.d8888f9630ed: Maps are scale drawings too. On this map one centimeter stands for five kilometers. The road from A to B measures five centimeters, so the real distance is five times five equals twenty-five kilometers.
math/scale-drawings.5f517984effe: A scale factor less than one shrinks the drawing. With k equals one over two, four becomes two and three becomes one point five. If k is greater than one it is an enlargement; if k is less than one it is a reduction.
math/scale-drawings.6aa0fa74fb91: With k equals three, each square becomes a three by three block of nine squares, so the area is nine times six equals fifty-four. Lengths grow by k, but areas grow by k times k equals k squared.
math/scale-drawings.790948d47251: Common mix-up: Lengths multiply by the scale factor k, but areas multiply by k squared. Triple the sides and the area becomes nine times as big, not three times. And stretching in only one direction is not scaling: the shape changes.
math/scale-drawings.5daa560b4ae2: Try it! A floor plan uses the scale one centimeter to two meters. A room is four centimeters by three centimeters on the plan, so it is really eight meters by six meters, with area forty-eight square meters. Check: twelve times two squared equals forty-eight.

math/similar-triangles.2c15a7b57fae: Angles A and D are both sixty-five degrees. Change angle E to match angle B. Write a similarity statement in matching vertex order. In A B C is similar to D E F, A matches D, B matches E, and C matches F, so A B matches D E, and so on.
math/similar-triangles.506d10948291: Two ratios are fixed at one point five. Change E F until the third side ratio matches. Write a similarity statement in matching vertex order. In A B C is similar to D E F, A matches D, B matches E, and C matches F, so A B matches D E, and so on.
math/similar-triangles.29b25fa116f9: Draw a line through the center O and each vertex. Multiply each distance from O by the same positive number k. In Basic mode, each image vertex stays on the same ray from O as its original. Corresponding angles match, and every side length scales by k. Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Perimeter is the sum of the sides, so it scales by k. The base and the height each scale by k, so area scales by k squared. When k equals one, the triangles are congruent and similar.

math/slope.6a88e19923f1: Start at a point on the line and walk to another one: three squares right, the run, then two squares up, the rise. We land back on the line.
math/slope.f55212ebce12: Where does the line start? It crosses the y-axis at the y-intercept b equals one. From there every three steps right add two, so y equals two over three, times x plus one. In general: y equals m x plus b
math/slope.83df4dda4333: If the line falls as you move right, the rise is negative, so the slope is negative. A horizontal line has rise zero, so m equals zero. A vertical line has run zero, and rise over zero is undefined.
math/slope.f1ad4c294017: A bigger slope makes a steeper line; a slope close to zero makes a flatter one. Watch the triangle stretch as m changes. Its run is two, and its rise is two m.
math/slope.7239a1bd26e0: Common mix-up: Slope is rise divided by run, vertical change divided by horizontal change, not the other way round. Subtract the y's and the x's in the same order. And keep these apart: a horizontal line has slope zero, but a vertical line's slope is undefined, you cannot divide by zero.
math/slope.7f787f74fb5d: That unchanging ratio is the slope, written m: m equals rise over run equals Delta y over Delta x equals y sub two minus y sub one, over x sub two minus x sub one. For our line m equals two over three: each one step right, it rises two over three.
math/slope.f4d68686c726: Worked example: find the line through the point one comma three and the point three comma seven. Slope: m equals the quantity seven minus three, over the quantity three minus one, which equals four over two, which equals two. Put one point in: three equals two times one plus b, so b equals one. The line is y equals two x plus one.
math/slope.e342d82ab024: Do it again, and again. From anywhere on the line, three right and two up lands you back on the line. The staircase steps are all identical.
math/slope.90c4f7166e3a: Now take a big step, six right, four up, and a tiny one, one point five right, one up. Different sizes, same shape: the triangles are similar, with the same angle. So the ratio rise divided by run never changes.

math/surface-volume.44e966b3bb07: The box is two units tall, so that layer repeats two times: twelve times two equals twenty-four cubes. The volume is twenty-four units cubed.
math/surface-volume.993b489549d3: Here is a box, a rectangular prism: four units long, three units wide and two units tall. How much space is inside it? To measure space, we first need a measuring tool.
math/surface-volume.75d6253a2c6e: Now fill a box that is two by one and a half by one with these half-size cubes: four times three times two equals twenty-four of them. Twenty-four times one eighth equals three, exactly what two times one and a half times one gives. The formula still works!
math/surface-volume.019a3ac98e36: A different question: how much paper covers the box? That is the surface area, the total area of all six faces. Cut along some edges and lay the box flat: this flat pattern is called a net.
math/surface-volume.7e27fb4dd858: What if an edge is a fraction, like one and a half? Cut a unit cube in half along every edge: you get eight small cubes with edge one half. Each is one eighth of the unit cube, and indeed one half times one half times one half equals one eighth.
math/surface-volume.ae3a9a1fa497: Try it: a cereal box is eight centimeters wide, three centimeters deep and twelve centimeters tall. V equals eight times three times twelve equals two hundred eighty-eight centimeters cubed of cereal fits inside, and S A equals two times the quantity twenty-four plus ninety-six plus thirty-six, equals three hundred twelve centimeters squared of cardboard wraps it.
math/surface-volume.04411a0976c3: Our measuring tool is the unit cube: every edge is one unit long. Its volume is one cubic unit, one unit cubed. Volume equals how many unit cubes it takes to fill a shape.
math/surface-volume.4f8c0546aa93: Fill the floor first. The bottom is four by three, so one layer holds four times three equals twelve cubes. That number is the area of the base: B equals twelve.
math/surface-volume.c808f508c551: The faces come in matching pairs: two four times three, two four times two, two three times two. Count the squares: two times twelve plus two times eight plus two times six equals fifty-two units squared. In general, S A equals two times the quantity l w plus l h plus w h.

math/systems.541fa06a5f14: A puzzle: you buy seven snacks and spend exactly ten dollars. Cookies cost one dollar each and juice boxes cost two dollars each. Call the number of cookies x and juice boxes y. A first guess, three cookies and four juice boxes, costs eleven dollars, too much!
math/systems.d4f59e40745c: Graphs can be hard to read exactly, so we also solve with algebra. Substitution: clue one says x equals seven minus y. Put that in place of x in clue two: seven minus y, plus two y equals ten, so y equals three, and then x equals four.
math/systems.80e44f7695e1: Which guess fits both clues? Only the point on both lines: where they cross, four, three. Check: four plus three equals seven and four plus two times three equals ten. So you bought four cookies and three juice boxes.
math/systems.06a3a7c0b948: Now use only the second clue, the cost: one dollar per cookie and two dollars per juice box gives x plus two y equals ten. Its guesses, zero, five; two, four; four, three… also line up, on a different line.
math/systems.52005c993e49: Elimination: stack the two clues as bars. Clue two has everything clue one has plus one more y, and its total is ten minus seven equals three bigger. Subtracting the equations cancels x and leaves y equals three.
math/systems.c291ed75eb13: Worked example: adult tickets cost five dollars, child tickets three dollars, and ten tickets cost thirty-eight dollars. Multiply the first equation by three and subtract: y cancels, leaving two x equals eight, so x equals four adults and y equals six children. Always check in both equations!
math/systems.1646152723e5: Use only the first clue, seven items: x plus y equals seven. Try every guess: zero cookies and seven juice boxes, one and six, two and five… Plot each guess as a point, x, y. They all land on one straight line!

math/transformations.0e435c9b19c9: Common mix-up: A ninety-degree counterclockwise rotation about the origin is x, y to minus y, x, not minus x, y; that one is a reflection across the y-axis. And a dilated figure is similar to the original but not congruent, unless the scale factor k equals one.
math/transformations.c502e6b73184: A dilation resizes. With center at the point zero comma zero and scale factor k equals one point five, every point slides along its ray from the origin until it is one point five times as far: from the point x comma y to the point one point five x comma one point five y. A factor k equals one half shrinks it instead.
math/transformations.0d08803c4530: Rotation, a turn, by ninety degrees counterclockwise about the origin. Follow B, four, one: it swings around to B prime, negative one, four. The coordinates swap places and the new first one changes sign: x, y to negative y, x.
math/transformations.08fa4b8b2c13: Worked example: which moves take A B C onto the pink triangle? It is upside down, so first reflect across the x-axis: x, y to x, negative y. Then slide six left: x, y to x minus six, y. Together: x, y to x minus six, negative y. Only rigid motions, so the triangles are congruent.
math/transformations.e7192bfdf74f: Translation, a slide: every point moves six left and four down. Watch the coordinates of A change: subtract six from x and four from y. Rule: x, y to x minus six, y minus four.
math/transformations.dca5d049467b: Here is triangle A B C on the coordinate grid: A, two, one. B, four, one. C, two, two. A transformation moves every point of a shape by the same rule. Let us slide it, flip it, turn it and resize it, and track the coordinates.
math/transformations.b229b9a73fd9: Compare the shapes. The angles stay the same, the right angle is still a right angle, and every side is multiplied by the same factor: three over two equals one point five over one equals one point five. Same shape, different size: similar, is similar to, not congruent.

math/triangles.ae547c9f2c6d: Equal sides in a triangle face equal angles. In Shape B, the angles opposite the two equal legs are both forty-five degrees.
math/triangles.9b85cb3ebbb9: Question one of two. Which set of sticks closes into a triangle with room inside?
math/triangles.aa0e0a7a4818: Bring the tips together and line up the edges. The three angles fill a straight angle of one hundred eighty degrees.
math/triangles.3d67240edbc2: Each pair of sides adds to more than the third because the direct segment is shorter than a detour. With a and b fixed, c is less than a plus b. The other two inequalities say c is greater than the absolute difference. With c too long the tips fall short. With c too short the shorter stick cannot reach the longer stick’s tip, even when the tips are as close as possible.

math/trig-ratios.e878621aab13: Draw the diagonal of a unit square. It splits a right angle in half, giving forty-five degrees. Both legs are one, so the Pythagorean theorem gives a diagonal of the square root of two.
math/trig-ratios.f7121a1252e7: Draw an altitude from the top of an equilateral triangle with side length two. It halves the sixty-degree top angle and the base. Each right triangle has a thirty-degree angle at the top and a sixty-degree angle at the base. The short leg is one. The other leg is the square root of the quantity two squared minus one squared equals the square root of three.

math/volume-solids.578c8ce6c270: Fill the sphere with water and pour it into the empty cylinder: it fills two thirds. The cone fills the last third. Cone to sphere to cylinder equals one to two to three, as Archimedes discovered over two thousand years ago.
math/volume-solids.e98fd9ff6080: Now stack twelve identical coins. Every layer has the same area pi r squared, and the layers pile up to a height h. So the volume of the stack is area of one layer times height.
math/volume-solids.9edc9ca1a5ac: Turn that into a formula. The sphere is two thirds of a cylinder with radius r and height two r: V sphere equals two thirds times pi r squared times two r equals four thirds times pi r cubed
math/volume-solids.6a65641cee85: So a cone holds one third of the cylinder with the same base and height: V cone equals one third times pi r squared h. A pyramid is one third of its prism for the same reason.
math/volume-solids.06065f2e72b9: Try it with r equals three centimeters and h equals six centimeters. Cylinder: fifty-four pi is about one hundred sixty-nine point six cubic centimeters. Cone: eighteen pi is about fifty-six point five cubic centimeters. Sphere: thirty-six pi is about one hundred thirteen point one cubic centimeters. And eighteen pi plus thirty-six pi equals fifty-four pi, just as the water showed.
math/volume-solids.57e673b2da8f: Now a ball, a sphere, of radius r. Our cylinder is exactly two r tall, so the ball fits perfectly inside: it touches the bottom, the top and the sides.
math/volume-solids.c60f05310ce0: Common mix-up: The formulas use the radius r, not the diameter, a ten centimeter diameter means r equals five centimeters. The height h of a cone is the straight-up height from the tip to the base, not the slanted length along its side.
math/volume-solids.78fe90911693: Let the water decide. Fill the cone, pour it into the cylinder, and repeat. It takes exactly three cones of water to fill the cylinder.

music/music-compose.90c0a43e2ac9: Motif. A tiny musical idea you can recognize. Often just two to six notes. Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony is built from a four-note motif: short, short, short, LONG.
music/music-compose.1854d64bfd00: Phrase. A musical sentence. Usually two or four bars long — about one breath of singing. Phrases end with a cadence, like sentences end with punctuation.
music/music-compose.5f8db4d43784: Chord and progression. Notes stacked together, then moving in order. A triad stacks one, three, five of a scale step. A progression is the order of chords — the song’s “road map.”
music/music-compose.55a13e60a7f5: Don't mix up: 起承转合 is about the shape of phrases, not a set of chords.
music/music-compose.33b3daf7a54c: 起承转合. The Chinese four-phrase plan. 起 begin, 承 continue, 转 turn, 合 close. Phrase two echoes phrase one, phrase three changes direction, phrase four brings it home. Many Chinese folk songs and poems follow it.

music/music-history.29f1d4e5c3ef: Film and game music. Nineteen thirties to today. Film scores use leitmotifs: a short theme for each character, an idea from Wagner’s operas. John Williams’ Star Wars brought back the full symphony orchestra to the movies in nineteen seventy-seven. Today game music adapts live to what the player does.
music/music-history.977238634163: Peking opera and pipa classics. Seventeen ninety, eighteen eighteen. Seventeen ninety: four opera troupes from Anhui came to Beijing for the emperor’s birthday — the start of Peking opera 京剧. Peking opera combines singing, speech, acting and acrobatics, led by the percussion band. The pipa epic 十面埋伏, “Ambush from Ten Sides,” about the battle of Gaixia, two hundred two B C E, was first printed in a pipa book in eighteen eighteen.
music/music-history.40a3305e1c07: Classical. Seventeen fifty to eighteen twenty. Haydn, “father of the symphony,” Mozart and young Beethoven. Clear, balanced melodies over simple accompaniments — elegant, like neat architecture. New forms: the symphony, the string quartet and sonata form.
music/music-history.bc37f08427ed: Ragtime, blues and jazz. Eighteen nineties to nineteen forties. Created by African American musicians, drawing on spirituals, work songs and West African rhythm. Scott Joplin’s “Maple Leaf Rag,” eighteen ninety-nine; the twelve-bar blues with “blue notes.” The first jazz record came out in nineteen seventeen; Louis Armstrong made improvised solos the star. Swing big bands, Duke Ellington, followed.
music/music-history.372814656406: Romantic. Eighteen twenty to nineteen hundred. Big feelings, bigger orchestras. Beethoven’s late works open the door. Chopin’s piano poetry, Tchaikovsky’s ballets, The Nutcracker, eighteen ninety-two. Composers celebrated their nations’ folk music, Dvořák, Grieg.
music/music-history.aeef944a3e0b: Don't mix up: Modern “classical” composers are still writing today — it did not end in eighteen twenty.
music/music-history.207d17148e76: Twentieth-century classical. Nineteen hundred to today. Debussy’s dreamy whole-tone colours; Stravinsky’s The Rite of Spring caused an uproar at its premiere in Paris in nineteen thirteen. Composers broke old rules: new scales, wild rhythms, electronic sounds. Minimalists such as Steve Reich and Philip Glass built music from short repeating patterns.
music/music-history.f99d80685696: Hip-hop. Nineteen seventy-three to today. August eleventh, nineteen seventy-three, the Bronx, New York: DJ Kool Herc loops the drum “breaks” of records at a party. Four elements: DJing, MCing, rapping, breakdancing and graffiti. Drum machines like the Roland T R eight zero eight and sampling made new beats — the same step-sequencer idea as our Rhythm lesson.
music/music-history.ff1e814ce021: Don't mix up: Guqin, seven strings, no bridges, is not equal to guzheng, twenty-one strings, bridges.
music/music-history.750f65f3ae5a: Bronze bells and the guqin. Circa four hundred thirty-three B C E. The sixty-five bells of Marquis Yi of Zeng show China had a full twelve-note system two thousand four hundred years ago. The legend of 伯牙 Boya and 钟子期 Zhong Ziqi: Boya played 高山流水, “High Mountains, Flowing Water,” and only his friend understood it. A true friend is still called 知音 — “one who knows the sound.” The guqin piece 流水 flew into space on Voyager in nineteen seventy-seven.
music/music-history.3d634c9969b9: Tang dynasty music. Six hundred eighteen to nine hundred seven. Chang’an was a world city: music arrived along the Silk Road from Central Asia, including the pipa. Emperor Xuanzong ran a music academy, the 梨园 “Pear Garden” — Chinese opera performers are still nicknamed “children of the Pear Garden.” Grand suites called 大曲 mixed music, song and dance.
music/music-history.ade44123e01f: East meets West. Nineteen fifty-nine to today. 梁祝 The Butterfly Lovers violin concerto puts Yue-opera melodies into a Western concerto. The concerto dates to nineteen fifty-nine and is by 何占豪 He Zhanhao and 陈钢 Chen Gang. Large Chinese orchestras mix erhu, pipa, dizi and percussion. In Chinese, those orchestras are called 民族管弦乐团. Tan Dun won the Oscar for best original score for Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, two thousand.
music/music-history.cec5b98e9150: Don't mix up: Baroque music used the harpsichord, not the modern piano, invented around seventeen hundred and common later.
music/music-history.6defa7a7dfbd: Baroque. Sixteen hundred to seventeen fifty. Opera is born in Italy around sixteen hundred. Bach, Vivaldi and Handel. Busy, interlocking melodies, counterpoint — like a fugue, where one tune chases itself. A harpsichord or organ plays the “basso continuo,” a non-stop bass line.
music/music-history.75424e62496d: New Chinese music. Nineteen twenties to nineteen forties. 刘天华 Liu Tianhua turned the erhu into a concert solo instrument. He lived from eighteen ninety-five to nineteen thirty-two. Blind street musician 阿炳 Abing, eighteen ninety-three to nineteen fifty: 二泉映月, recorded in nineteen fifty. 聂耳 Nie Er’s 义勇军进行曲 March of the Volunteers became the national anthem of the PRC. March of the Volunteers dates to nineteen thirty-five. 冼星海 Xian Xinghai’s 黄河大合唱 Yellow River Cantata rallied people during the War of Resistance. Yellow River Cantata dates to nineteen thirty-nine.
music/music-history.ac62a5ffe11e: Don't mix up: 义勇军进行曲 was written for a nineteen thirty-five film, years before it became the anthem.
music/music-history.d5099faf0587: Don't mix up: “Classical music,” any orchestral music, versus the Classical period, seventeen fifty to eighteen twenty.

music/music-instruments.5144647bdc31: Timpani. Percussion, tuned drums. A pedal stretches the drumhead tighter to raise the pitch. Usually two to five drums per player. Tighter head, faster vibration, higher pitch, just like the string lab!

music/music-instruments.0b640f3b0483: Tanggu and gong 堂鼓, 锣. Percussion, the energy of festivals and opera. 堂鼓: a barrel drum played with two sticks. The gong 锣 and cymbals 镲 add crashes; in Peking opera the percussion section leads the whole show. Drum and gong patterns are called 锣鼓经.

Also links to Grade eight physics “sound phenomena”, pitch, loudness, timbre; frequency and vibration.
music/music-instruments.6393dc2da82f: The real thing. A pipa, pear-shaped lute, in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
music/music-instruments.a61804827ef2: Bone flutes found at Jiahu, 贾湖, Henan, are about eight thousand to nine thousand years old.
music/music-instruments.29ca3b91efde: Violin. Strings, the orchestra’s melody voice. Four strings tuned G, D, A, E, each a fifth apart. The bow is horsehair rubbed with rosin so it grips the string. A full orchestra has about thirty violins, in “first” and “second” groups.
music/music-instruments.a625de418c1c: Dizi 笛子. Winds, bamboo flute. A bamboo transverse flute with six finger holes. Its secret: an extra hole covered with a thin membrane 笛膜 that buzzes — the bright, reedy sound. Bone flutes found at Jiahu, 贾湖, Henan, are about eight thousand to nine thousand years old.
music/music-instruments.191a6958ea43: Sheng 笙. Winds, mouth organ with free reeds. A bundle of bamboo pipes, each with a small metal reed. It can play chords — rare for a wind instrument. It is about three thousand years old. It appears in the 诗经 Book of Songs. The free-reed idea later inspired the harmonica and the accordion.
music/music-instruments.36d1993e16ad: Memory hint: Bai Juyi’s poem 琵琶行: “big pearls, small pearls, falling on a jade plate” — that is the pipa’s sound.

music/music-instruments.ab1bea62e17f: Guzheng 古筝. Plucked strings, zither with moving bridges. Usually twenty-one strings, each with its own movable bridge. Tuned to the pentatonic scale, 宫商角徵羽, so sweeping glissandos always sound good. Pressing the string left of the bridge bends the pitch up — that adds the “missing” notes. Its ancestor, the 秦筝, is more than two thousand years old.

music/music-instruments.69b697493017: A string’s frequency is: f equals one divided by the quantity two L, times the square root of the quantity T divided by mu. L equals length, T equals tension, mu equals mass per metre. Move the sliders, pluck, and tune to the target note, within plus or minus ten cents. Then lightly touch the string at one half or one third — those are harmonics.

music/music-instruments.74a4a7c0af33: A Western orchestra has four families: strings, woodwinds, brass and percussion. A Chinese orchestra has four sections too: bowed strings, plucked strings, winds and percussion. Click an instrument to hear it and read its story. Explore eight or more for stars.

music/music-instruments.ea206ee54d98: Erhu 二胡. Bowed strings, the “Chinese violin”. Just two strings, tuned D four and A four — a fifth apart. The bow hair runs BETWEEN the two strings. No fingerboard: fingers press the strings in mid-air, so slides and wide vibrato are easy. Famous piece: 二泉映月, “The Moon Reflected in Erquan Spring” by the blind street musician 阿炳 Abing, eighteen ninety-three to nineteen fifty.
music/music-instruments.c450ab425131: French horn. Brass, mellow and round. About three point seven meters of tubing wound into a circle, or about twelve feet of tubing. The player puts a hand inside the bell to shape the sound. Its bell points backward.

music/music-instruments.a189c0f18db7: A violin and an erhu play the same note — A four, four hundred forty vibrations a second — yet you can tell them apart instantly. Why? The secret is in the harmonics: every instrument has its own sound fingerprint, called timbre.

music/music-pitch.4af44997d30a: Octave. Double the frequency. Go up twelve half steps, eight letter names, and the frequency doubles: A four, four hundred forty hertz. A five, eight hundred eighty hertz. That is why notes repeat their names every octave.
music/music-pitch.16aec3e49448: 五声音阶 pentatonic. Five notes: 宫 商 角 徵 羽. 宫 gōng, 商 shāng, 角 jué, 徵 zhǐ, 羽 yǔ equals one, two, three, five, six, do re mi sol la. No half steps, so any combination sounds smooth — it is the base of most Chinese folk music, and also of blues, Scottish and West African tunes.
music/music-pitch.b1eeb28c1089: Don't mix up: 徵 is read zhǐ here, not zhēng, and 角 is jué, not jiǎo.
music/music-pitch.b7e6e45a5b04: Don't mix up: 简谱 numbers are scale degrees, not fixed pitches — one is not always C.
music/music-pitch.7a23e8e651e5: Interval. The distance between two notes. Count letter names, including both ends: C to G equals C D E F G equals a fifth. Small whole-number frequency ratios sound smooth: octave two to one, fifth three to two.
music/music-pitch.93522c381a9f: Staff and clefs. A map for pitch. Higher on the staff equals higher pitch. Treble clef, G clef, curls around G four; bass clef, F clef, has two dots around F three.
music/music-pitch.2d3ec38021f3: Pitch and frequency. How high or low a sound is. Pitch depends on frequency: vibrations per second, measured in hertz, H Z. A four equals four hundred forty hertz is the tuning note orchestras use.
music/music-pitch.82649ce225a9: 简谱 numbered notation. Numbers instead of dots on lines. One to seven equals do to ti; dots above or below change the octave; zero is a rest. The idea came from France and reached China through Japan around nineteen hundred in the school-song movement 学堂乐歌. In France, Rousseau proposed numbers in seventeen forty-two.
music/music-pitch.08dcadc055d6: Don't mix up: A “third” spans three letter names but only four, major, or three, minor, half steps.
music/music-pitch.e0696147db41: Don't mix up: An octave has eight letter names but twelve half steps.

music/music-rhythm.e27c6f1cdf17: Presto. Very fast. Italian for “quickly.” At two hundred BPM a beat lasts only zero point three seconds!
music/music-rhythm.f78002d958d7: Resting heart rate. Your body’s own beat. A normal adult resting heart beats sixty to one hundred times a minute. Kids’ hearts beat a bit faster; exercise can push it above one hundred fifty.
music/music-rhythm.9d33dc0a6b6c: Meter and time signature. How beats are grouped. Top number: beats per measure. Bottom: which note gets the beat, four equals quarter. Two four, march. Three four, waltz. Four four, most pop. Six eight equals two big beats of three.
music/music-rhythm.2b68ce089c7e: Tempo. How fast the beat goes. Measured in BPM — beats per minute. Sixty BPM equals one beat per second.
music/music-rhythm.b0d3e6d4ab84: Moderato. Moderate. Neither fast nor slow. Many marches sit around one hundred ten to one hundred twenty BPM.
music/music-rhythm.b80feebb72f8: Andante. A walking pace. From the Italian for “to walk.” Most people walk at roughly one hundred to one hundred twenty steps a minute.
music/music-rhythm.71ee578144eb: 板眼. Chinese words for strong and weak beats. In Chinese opera and folk music, 板 is the strong beat, 眼 a weak beat. 一板一眼 equals two four, 一板三眼 equals four four, 有板无眼 equals one four, 散板 equals free time with no fixed beat.
music/music-rhythm.09d16631d83c: Don't mix up: six eighths is not “three quarters doubled”: six eighths feels like two big beats, three quarters feels like three.
music/music-rhythm.3074314498fa: Don't mix up: In 京剧 Peking opera the 板 is marked by the clapper 板 itself — a real wooden instrument!

physics/electric-power.fabdc360d1ac: Electric power, 电功率, is how fast electrical energy is transferred. One watt is one joule per second. Rated power is the power a device uses in normal operation at its rated voltage. Actual power is the power it uses under its current operating conditions.

physics/electricity.1b7e9ee361e8: Electrons, moving charge. Tiny negative charges that flow in metal wires. The blue dots are electrons. They flow from the minus terminal, through the circuit, to the plus terminal. Scientists draw “conventional current” the other way, from plus to minus. That rule was chosen before electrons were discovered. The dots move faster when the current is bigger. Real electrons drift slowly, but the whole wire is full of them, so they all start moving together and the bulb lights instantly.
physics/electricity.add7df3286f3: Battery, cells. The energy source that pushes charges around the loop. Voltage, measured in volts, V, is the “push” a battery gives to charges. Each cell here gives one point five volts. Cells joined end-to-end, in series, add up: three cells equals four point five volts. Inside the battery, chemical energy is changed into electrical energy. Electrons leave the negative, minus, terminal, travel around the circuit, and return to the positive, plus, terminal.

physics/energy.211e11e65aad: Kinetic energy. Energy of motion. KE equals one half times m times v squared, half times mass times speed squared. Speed counts the most: twice the speed, FOUR times the KE. The cart has the most KE at the lowest point of the track, where it is fastest.
physics/energy.69d53275f194: Conservation of energy. The total never changes. Mechanical energy equals KE plus PE. Law of conservation of energy: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another. On this coaster: KE plus GPE plus elastic PE plus thermal energy equals the energy the lift motor put in.
physics/energy.2a0f78417ada: Gravitational potential energy. Energy stored by height. GPE equals m times g times h, mass times nine point eight newtons per kilogram times height. Units: joules, J. Twice the height, twice the GPE. Twice the mass, twice the GPE. The cart has the most GPE at the top of the start hill, where it is moving slowest.
physics/energy.196ded15f25a: Reference level, h equals zero. Where we measure height from. Gravitational PE is measured from a chosen reference level. Here it is the ground. At the ground, h equals zero, so GPE equals zero joules. You may choose any reference level, but you must use the same one for the whole problem.

physics/formula-sheet.60fe0417e494: Wave speed. Wavelength is the distance between neighboring crests. In a fixed medium with a fixed wave speed, increasing frequency shortens the wavelength. For light in vacuum, v is about three point zero times ten to the eighth meters per second.
physics/formula-sheet.7e426b7793dc: Electrical work from voltage and current. Use constant voltage and current. Volts times amps times seconds gives joules. The billing unit is kilowatt-hours, and one kilowatt-hour equals three point six times ten to the sixth joules.
physics/formula-sheet.3adb45efd8f9: Voltage division in series. The same current flows through both resistors. For nonzero voltage drops, U one over U two equals R one over R two. If both voltages are zero, the voltages alone give no resistance ratio.
physics/formula-sheet.33e8296657d6: Current division in parallel. Both resistors have the same voltage across them. For nonzero branch currents, I one over I two equals R two over R one. If both currents are zero, the currents alone give no resistance ratio.
physics/formula-sheet.ab10af00c76d: Convex lens, real image. This positive-distance form models a thin converging lens with a real image. The object must be farther from the lens than its focal length. At u equals two f the image is real, inverted and the same size.
physics/formula-sheet.641f8b88a5af: Electric power. Use the device’s actual terminal voltage and current. Rated power applies at the rated operating conditions. Average power is W over t.
physics/formula-sheet.6bbe7f228cde: Celsius and kelvin. Apply the offset to a temperature reading. For a change in temperature, an interval of one degree Celsius equals one kelvin.
physics/formula-sheet.d373722cea97: Energy from meter pulses. If the meter constant is given in pulses per kilowatt-hour, impulses per kilowatt-hour, or turns per kilowatt-hour, revolutions per kilowatt-hour, the quotient is in kilowatt-hours. Count the pulses or complete turns during the interval.
physics/formula-sheet.6c01cd2e1105: Contact pressure. Use the actual contact area and the perpendicular force. One square centimeter equals zero point zero zero zero one square meters.

physics/heat-transfer.f7adb9f28450: Radiation, glowing coil. Heat carried by electromagnetic waves. The red-hot coil gives off infrared radiation in all directions — hold your hand beside it, never on it, and you feel the warmth. Radiation needs no matter. That is how the Sun’s energy crosses one hundred fifty million kilometers of empty space to reach Earth. Dark, dull surfaces absorb radiation well; shiny, light surfaces reflect it.
physics/heat-transfer.9825f097fd48: Thermometer, temperature. Measures how hot or cold. Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of the particles in a substance. Faster particles equals higher temperature. Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius and freezes at zero degrees Celsius, at sea level. The liquid in the thermometer expands when it warms up, so it rises up the tube.
physics/heat-transfer.e877e4afdd31: Steam, thermal energy. Energy of moving particles. Thermal energy is the total kinetic energy of all the particles in an object. As the water gains thermal energy its molecules move faster. The fastest ones escape from the surface as water vapour. When boiling, the extra energy breaks the water molecules apart from each other instead of raising the temperature, so boiling water stays at one hundred degrees Celsius.

physics/lenses.891748e298a1: A camera lens system converges light. Here u equals sixty centimeters and f equals fifteen centimeters, so the object is beyond two F. The image is real, inverted, and smaller. Move the sensor until the rays meet on it. Dashed lines show where the rays would go without the sensor in the way.

physics/light.2806d88a8c63: Common mix-up: Rotate the mirror by ten degrees and the reflected ray turns by twenty degrees, because both angles change.
physics/light.82d6f09929d0: Laser, light source. Makes a narrow, straight beam of light. Light is an electromagnetic wave. It needs no air or water to travel, so sunlight can cross empty space to reach us. In one material, light travels in straight lines. We draw these paths as rays with arrows. Light is the fastest thing in the universe: about three hundred thousand kilometers every second in a vacuum.
physics/light.def788db9284: Normal line. An imaginary line at ninety degrees to the surface. The dashed yellow line is the normal. It is drawn wherever light hits a surface. The angle of incidence, i, and the angle of reflection or refraction, r, are measured from the normal. A ray that travels exactly along the normal does not bend when it enters glass.
physics/light.17afd7602a1b: Light ray. A model of the path light takes. The moving dots show the direction light travels. When light meets matter it can be reflected, bounce, refracted or transmitted, pass through and bend, or absorbed, turned into heat. You see an object when light from it, made or reflected, enters your eyes.
physics/light.e510675c6232: Glass block. Refraction: light bends when its speed changes. Light slows from about three hundred thousand kilometers per second in air to about two hundred thousand kilometers per second in glass. Entering glass, fast, slow, the ray bends TOWARD the normal. Leaving, slow, fast, it bends AWAY. With parallel sides, the ray comes out parallel to the way it went in, just shifted sideways. If light inside glass hits the surface at a big angle, more than about forty-two degrees, it cannot escape: total internal reflection. Optical fibers use this.

physics/magnetism.84683d77a5dd: Iron core, nail. Makes the coil’s field much stronger. Iron inside the coil becomes magnetized and adds its own field. An iron core can make an electromagnet hundreds of times stronger. This model uses ten times. Soft iron loses its magnetism quickly when the current stops, which is perfect for an electromagnet.

physics/measurements-density.a472fb8ae4da: Near zero degrees Celsius, ice has a more open structure than liquid water. The same mass takes up about nine percent more space when frozen. That is why ice floats and freezing water can crack a rigid, full container.
physics/measurements-density.7bf52e1b0299: Question one of twelve. In the cylinder model, the water reads thirty-eight milliliters at eye level. You read the meniscus from above. How does the apparent reading compare?
physics/measurements-density.983d198a7584: The model uses one point zero zero grams per milliliter for water and zero point nine zero grams per milliliter for oil. The liquids stay in layers, so their volumes add. At equal volumes, the average density is halfway between their densities. If volume changes on mixing, use the measured final volume.
physics/measurements-density.c855d96549e0: The mass lost by the beaker is the sixty grams gained by the cylinder. The drops behind stay in the second weighing.
physics/measurements-density.761216fe328b: For water, line up your eye with the lowest point. One milliliter equals one cubic centimeter.
physics/measurements-density.a1e2b656b2b8: Question one of two. A uniform fifty-four gram metal sample has a volume of twenty cubic centimeters. Which reference metal is the best match?

If the test ball has less mass, divide its mass by aluminum’s density to find the volume of metal. Subtract that from the outer volume to find the cavity. The model ignores the mass of the trapped air.
physics/measurements-density.63eec5076dd4: Liquid density is often given in grams per milliliter. Its numerical value is the same in grams per cubic centimeter because one milliliter equals one cubic centimeter.

Put the object on the left. Use tweezers to try weights on the right, largest first, then move the rider. Once balanced, add the weights’ masses and the rider reading.

physics/measurements-density.b967562a59c0: The density is two point seven zero grams per cubic centimeter. Aluminum is the closest match in the table.
physics/measurements-density.4d28d78ad07e: On U.S. food packages, an ounce, O Z, measures mass. One ounce is about twenty-eight point three five grams. On drink bottles, a U.S. fluid ounce, F L O Z, measures volume. One U.S. fluid ounce is about twenty-nine point five seven milliliters.
physics/measurements-density.a5bdb89bbbcc: Question one of two. Mix thirty milliliters of water and seventy milliliters of oil in the model. What is their average density?

If you zero the balance with the rider at one point two grams and later add the full rider reading, the result will be one point two grams too high. Use a container for liquids and stay within the balance’s capacity.
physics/measurements-density.83f868b3c068: Try sixty milliliters of water and forty milliliters of oil. The total mass is sixty grams plus thirty-six grams — equals ninety-six grams. Divide by one hundred milliliters to get zero point nine six grams per milliliter.
physics/measurements-density.53530c0af76f: Set the cylinder on a flat surface. Read water at the bottom of its curved surface, the meniscus, with your eye at the same height. Find the value of one division first. Each small mark is two milliliters here and the parallax effect is exaggerated.
physics/measurements-density.33378b294dd3: Beaker plus liquid left behind, m two
physics/measurements-density.1799e98e260b: Find the volume of a stone by water displacement, 排水法. Compare the two measurement orders.
physics/measurements-density.14951ff40155: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram, K G. Grams, G, are also common. One kilogram equals one thousand grams. Measure weight in newtons, N.
physics/measurements-density.f3bb77fb8d58: A sealed aluminum ball has an outer volume of one hundred cubic centimeters and a mass of two hundred sixteen grams. Ignoring the mass of the air inside, how much space is hollow?
physics/measurements-density.797f6c3d6aae: Two points for the same uniform material are ten cubic centimeters, twenty-seven grams — and thirty cubic centimeters, eighty-one grams. Use both points to find its density.
physics/measurements-density.67c382c337ef: Question one of two. Convert two point seven zero grams per cubic centimeter to kilograms per cubic meter.
physics/measurements-density.e08d8c762aa6: Density, 密度, is mass per unit volume. With volume on the horizontal axis and mass on the vertical axis, the slope is density. For a uniform substance at the same temperature and pressure, a larger sample has proportionally more mass and the same density.

physics/mechanical-motion.1837a101d94a: Given. The ramp is one point zero zero meter long. The front reaches B at two point zero zero seconds and C at two point eight zero seconds. The lower half is zero point five zero meters.
physics/mechanical-motion.04ca213106e7: Mechanical motion is a change in position over time relative to a reference object, 参照物. On a moving train, a seated passenger is at rest relative to the train and moving relative to the platform.
physics/mechanical-motion.12bb8ed27e6b: Three measurements of the same time interval give two point nine six seconds, three point zero three seconds, and three point zero one seconds. Add them and divide by the number of trials.

physics/mechanical-motion.7574500dfaea: Remember: On the same distance-time axes, a steeper slope means faster motion. Multiply meters per second by three point six to get kilometers per hour. Divide by three point six to go back.

Giving both speeds equal weight would give zero point two two five meters per second, which differs from the overall average speed.

physics/mechanical-motion.12591572b06f: Use about three hundred forty meters per second for the speed of sound in air at room temperature. The sound travels to the wall and back, covering the one-way distance twice.

physics/mechanical-motion.267c69db5852: A: six meters per second right, B: two meters per second right, Gap: twenty-four point zero zero meters
physics/mechanical-motion.bc5b3a31bba2: Question one of two. A train travels to the right. What does a seated passenger see the platform do?
physics/mechanical-motion.aa919eee4e83: In U.S. customary units, one inch equals exactly two point five four centimeters.
physics/mechanical-motion.9571ebfb496a: Mean reading: two point one two seconds

physics/mechanical-motion.0d8514d00c78: Answer. The average speed is five meters per second, or eighteen kilometers per hour. U.S. road signs commonly use miles per hour. One mile per hour is about one point six one kilometers per hour.

physics/motion.e689011cb7fd: Velocity. Speed in a direction. Velocity is speed together with its direction, for example ten meters per second east. The green arrow above each car shows its velocity: a longer arrow means faster, and it points the way the car moves. When a car reverses, its velocity becomes negative: the arrow flips to point backwards.
physics/motion.6fa1cf86ea85: Speed. How fast: distance divided by time. Speed equals distance divided by time. The SI unit is meters per second, meters per second. Average speed equals total distance divided by total time. Instantaneous speed is the speed at one moment, like a speedometer reading. Ten meters per second is thirty-six kilometers per hour, about as fast as a quick bicycle.
physics/motion.b6d41af05083: Common mix-up: A car driving around a curve at a steady twenty meters per second has a constant speed but a CHANGING velocity, because its direction keeps changing.
physics/motion.ddcc1d738af4: Acceleration. How fast velocity changes. Acceleration equals change in velocity divided by time: a equals the quantity v end minus v start, divided by t. Unit: meters per second squared, meters per second, every second. a equals two point five meters per second squared means the velocity grows by two point five meters per second every second. Slowing down is also acceleration, pointing backwards, negative. Turning is acceleration too.
physics/motion.7eca254420a9: Common mix-up: Speed has no direction. Ten meters per second north and ten meters per second south are the same SPEED but different VELOCITIES.
physics/motion.1f70c606ee2e: Common mix-up: Run one four hundred meter lap and stop where you began: distance equals four hundred meters, displacement equals zero meters. Turn on “Allow reversing” to see this on the track.
physics/motion.7f3559433bad: Displacement. Change in position, with a direction. Displacement tells how far and in which direction you end up from your starting point. The cyan arrow on the track points from the start line to each car: that is the car’s displacement. If you come back to where you started, your displacement is zero meters, even though your distance is not.
physics/motion.7cb98932301a: Common mix-up: Acceleration does not mean “going fast”. A car cruising at a steady thirty meters per second has ZERO acceleration.
physics/motion.59b7f3e6008d: Distance. How much ground is covered. Distance is the total length of the path an object travels. Its SI unit is the meter, meter. Distance never goes down: even driving backwards adds to it, like a car’s odometer. The marker posts on this track are ten meters apart, and the whole strip is one hundred meters long.

physics/newtons-laws.7197eb7b86a3: Action-reaction pair, third law. Forces always come in equal, opposite pairs. Newton’s third law: when object A pushes on object B, B pushes back on A with a force of equal size in the opposite direction. The spring pushes the left cart left with forty newtons and the right cart right with forty newtons, at the same time. Equal forces, but the lighter cart gets the bigger acceleration, a equals F divided by m, so it speeds away faster.
physics/newtons-laws.268083c893a0: Mass. Amount of matter equals amount of inertia. Mass is how much matter an object has, measured in kilograms, kilograms. Each gray block on a cart is one kilogram. More mass means more inertia: it is harder to speed up, slow down or turn. With the same force, a four kilogram cart gets only one quarter of the acceleration of a one kilogram cart.
physics/newtons-laws.c8aeedadd89c: Inertia, first law. Objects keep doing what they are doing. Newton’s first law: an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion keeps moving at the same speed and direction, unless an unbalanced force acts on it. Inertia is this tendency to resist changes in motion. More mass equals more inertia. In the fast yank, the cloth’s friction acts for only a fraction of a second, so the dishes barely move.
physics/newtons-laws.6f946bb42fed: Weight, gravity. W equals m times g. Weight is the force of gravity on a mass: W equals m times g. On Earth g equals nine point eight newtons per kilogram. The spring scale holds a one kilogram mass: it reads nine point eight newtons on Earth, one point six newtons on the Moon, twenty-four point eight newtons on Jupiter. Mass, kilograms, stays the same everywhere; weight, newtons, changes with the planet.
physics/newtons-laws.d013d77355a6: Friction from the cloth. The only sideways force on the dishes. Friction between cloth and dish can give the dish at most about mu times g, about zero point five times nine point eight, about four point nine meters per second squared of acceleration. Pull the cloth more gently than that and the dishes ride along with it, and fall off the edge! Yank harder and the cloth slides out from under them; the dishes only get a short, weak tug.
physics/newtons-laws.a627ec5952bd: Acceleration. a equals F divided by m. The orange arrow appears only while the push acts: acceleration happens only when there is a net force. a equals ten newtons divided by two kilograms equals five meters per second squared. The velocity grows by five meters per second every second of pushing. Acceleration is always in the same direction as the net force.
physics/newtons-laws.6c4647c0012f: Common mix-up: When the push stops, the cart does NOT stop. On a frictionless track it keeps rolling at a constant velocity, first law.
physics/newtons-laws.aa7b7344a498: Net force, the push. An unbalanced force changes motion. Force is a push or a pull, measured in newtons, newtons. One newton is about the weight of a small apple. The red arrow is the push. It lasts zero point five seconds; after that the net force is zero. Newton’s second law: F equals m times a, so a equals F divided by m. Double the force, double the acceleration.

physics/ohms-law.829e5bfc6605: Ohm’s law is written I equals U over R. At constant resistance, current is proportional to voltage. At a fixed voltage, current is inversely proportional to resistance. A bulb’s filament usually gets hotter as the voltage rises, so its resistance increases. The dashed curve is an illustrative model.

physics/phase-changes.4bece561e69f: At one atmosphere, pure ice melts at about zero degrees Celsius, thirty-two degrees Fahrenheit, and pure water boils at about one hundred degrees Celsius, two hundred twelve degrees Fahrenheit. On each plateau, the sample still absorbs heat. The share of the mass in each phase changes while the temperature stays steady. At the same pressure, pure water freezes at about zero degrees Celsius and releases heat as it freezes.
physics/phase-changes.51b60b8a0cea: Estimate the temperature and choose a suitable range. Check the unit and the value of one small division. Each small interval here is two degrees Celsius. Fully immerse the bulb in the liquid. Keep the bulb clear of the container’s bottom and sides. Wait for the reading to stabilize. Keep the bulb immersed and read with your eyes level with the top of the liquid column.

physics/pressure.2dfb0e2f217f: Water pushes on the probe’s flexible membrane and raises the air pressure in the hose. The water falls on the connected side and rises on the open side. Read the vertical difference delta H. In this ideal model, both liquids are water, so delta H equals the probe depth.
physics/pressure.452f0a0166d1: Average pressure, 压强, is perpendicular force F divided by contact area S. The force acts at right angles to the surface. Keep the force fixed and compare the marks made by the three faces.

physics/simple-machines.9a5795c55af4: Pulley. A grooved wheel with a rope. A fixed pulley, attached to the ceiling, only changes the direction of your pull: MA equals one. A movable pulley rides up with the load and halves the force: MA equals two. A block and tackle combines pulleys: MA equals the number of rope strands holding up the load.
physics/simple-machines.43827a5f5046: Mechanical advantage and work. How many times a machine multiplies your force. Mechanical advantage, MA, equals output force divided by input force. MA four means one hundred newtons of effort lifts a four hundred newton load. Work equals force times distance, measured in joules, joules. One joule equals one newton times one meter. With MA four you pull four meters of rope to lift the load one meter: the work is the same, ideal machine.
physics/simple-machines.cb968e57239e: Lever. A rigid bar that turns on a fulcrum. A lever is a stiff bar that pivots on a point called the fulcrum. Class one: fulcrum in the middle, seesaw, crowbar, scissors. Class two: load in the middle, wheelbarrow, bottle opener. Class three: effort in the middle, tweezers, broom, your forearm. Law of the lever: effort times effort arm equals load times load arm.
physics/simple-machines.e7b4a2b71bd5: Common mix-up: Machines do NOT reduce the work you do! If a machine cuts your force to one quarter, you must move four times as far. Work equals force times distance stays the same, ideally; in real life friction makes it a little more.
physics/simple-machines.d72b6dadaa3f: Common mix-up: Not every lever makes work easier on your muscles. A class three lever needs MORE force than the load, but the load end moves farther and faster.
physics/simple-machines.320e4478a204: Common mix-up: No machine gives more work out than you put in. Real machines lose some work to friction, so efficiency is always below one hundred percent.
physics/simple-machines.1f0c046ac907: Inclined plane. A ramp: less force over a longer distance. An inclined plane is a flat sloping surface, like a ramp. Pushing a load up a ramp takes less force than lifting it straight up, but you move it farther. Ideal MA equals ramp length divided by height. A four meter ramp up to one meter has MA four.
physics/simple-machines.675a5c84f9e2: Load and load arm. The weight you want to move. The load, resistance, is the force the machine works against, here the weight of the crate: W equals m times g. The load arm is the distance from the fulcrum to the load. A twenty kilogram crate weighs twenty times nine point eight equals one hundred ninety-six newtons.

physics/sound.37b85e5a1e4e: Air molecules, the medium. Pass the vibration along. Sound is a mechanical wave: it needs a medium — a solid, liquid or gas — to travel through. Each molecule just jiggles back and forth around its place and bumps the next one. The molecules do not fly from the speaker to your ear. Sound travels faster in liquids and fastest in solids, because their particles are closer together: air about three hundred forty-three meters per second, water about one thousand four hundred eighty meters per second, steel about five thousand nine hundred sixty meters per second.
physics/sound.3a403e374348: Ear canal. Carries sound to the eardrum. The ear canal is a tube about two point five centimeters long that leads from the outer ear to the eardrum. It contains earwax, which traps dust and protects the ear. Never push objects into your ear canal: you could damage the eardrum.
physics/sound.4bb21f5af47d: Ossicles, hammer, anvil, stirrup. Amplify the vibrations. Three tiny bones in the middle ear: the hammer, malleus, anvil, incus, and stirrup, stapes. They act like levers, passing the vibrations from the eardrum to the cochlea and making them stronger. The stirrup is the smallest bone in the human body — about three millimeters long.

physics/specific-heat.46cd07035ad5: The exhaust valve opens and the intake valve stays closed. The rising piston pushes burned gases out of the cylinder. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice per cycle, or seven hundred twenty degrees, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.e974bf6fda99: The intake valve opens and the exhaust valve stays closed. The piston moves down, drawing an air-fuel mixture into the cylinder. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice per cycle, or seven hundred twenty degrees, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.d58717832944: Temperature. A measure of how hot or cold something is. At a higher temperature, particles generally move more vigorously. Even particles in a solid keep vibrating. Internal energy, nèinéng. Add the energy from particles’ motion to the potential energy from their interactions to get the object’s internal energy. Internal energy depends on factors such as temperature, mass, and state. Ice has internal energy, too. Heat, rèliàng. Energy transferred because of a temperature difference, measured in joules, joules. The net transfer by heat is from higher to lower temperature. Molecules are always moving randomly. During diffusion, kuòsàn, 扩散, particles move in all directions, with an overall spread from higher to lower concentration. They keep moving after the gases are mixed. Molecules also exert forces on one another. At very close range they repel, and at somewhat greater distances attraction can hold them together.
physics/specific-heat.3887c10466fd: A fuel’s heating value, rèzhí, 热值, q, is the energy released per unit mass in complete combustion, measured in joules per kilogram. Use the heating value given in a calculation problem. Efficiency eta is useful work W divided by the energy Q released by complete combustion. The remaining energy still counts in the total. Much of it leaves in hot exhaust or through the cooling system. Friction also converts some mechanical energy into internal energy.
physics/specific-heat.6e2c3f632383: Both valves stay closed. Combustion raises the gas temperature and pressure. The expanding gas pushes the piston down and does work on it, turning the crankshaft. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice per cycle, or seven hundred twenty degrees, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.
physics/specific-heat.97e117b5a7c7: People’s Education Press, Grade nine physics contents
physics/specific-heat.ea1f913e6462: Specific heat capacity, bǐrèróng, 比热容, c, is the energy needed to warm one kilogram of a material by one degree Celsius. We use about four thousand two hundred joules per kilogram degree Celsius for water and about eight hundred joules per kilogram degree Celsius for dry sand. For equal masses given equal energy, the sample with the larger c warms less.
physics/specific-heat.b3cb6f9112a1: Both valves are closed. The piston moves up and does work on the mixture, raising its pressure and temperature. The spark plug fires near the end. This is a simplified spark-ignition gasoline engine. The crankshaft turns twice per cycle, or seven hundred twenty degrees, and expanding gases drive the piston during the power stroke. A flywheel and other rotating parts help carry the engine through the other strokes.

physics/static-charge.4a326f39ff2a: Charge is written as Q. Its SI unit is the coulomb, C. A nanocoulomb, N C, is one billionth of a coulomb. A and B are the two objects. Each rub transfers one nanocoulomb of negative charge in this model. The moving symbol represents a group of electrons.
physics/static-charge.a5c80c0e2639: Question one of two. Thunder sounds while you are outside. Where should you go?
physics/static-charge.a86dbc541ae8: Question one of two. What makes copper a good conductor?
physics/static-charge.c8cc2151672c: Have students record what they observe and what they infer. Compare the electroscope readings in step two and the final induction step to see that leaf separation can result from redistribution or net charge. Every activity can be completed on the page.
physics/static-charge.24cdce7e06fc: Given, A balloon and hair start neutral and exchange no charge with their surroundings. After rubbing, the balloon has a charge of minus four nanocoulombs.
physics/static-charge.612b63cd0363: Go straight into a sturdy enclosed building. If none is nearby, get into a car with a metal roof and close the windows. Wait at least thirty minutes after the last thunder before going back outside. Indoors, stay away from doors, windows, plumbing, and plugged-in equipment.
physics/static-charge.d451a055b634: Field-line arrows show which way a positive test charge is pushed or pulled. They point away from a positive source and toward a negative source. Move the test charge farther away and watch the force arrow below it get shorter. The reading compares its force to the force at four centimeters, just like the earlier graph.

physics/waves.32c4ff092d4e: Amplitude. How big the vibration is. Amplitude is the distance from the rest position to a crest, or to a trough. Bigger amplitude equals more energy. The energy grows with the amplitude squared: double A, four times the energy. For sound, larger amplitude means louder; for light, brighter; for water, taller waves.
physics/waves.aa525c2e8fd7: Vibrating source, frequency. Where every wave begins. Every wave starts with a vibration: a hand shaking a rope, a speaker cone, a pebble dropped in a pond. Frequency, f, is the number of complete waves made — or passing a point — each second. Unit: hertz, hertz. One hertz equals one wave per second. Period T equals one divided by f is the time for one complete wave. Wave speed v equals f times lambda.

physics/work-power.8bfd897ce897: Trace the rope and count the n segments that pull upward directly on the load or moving block. The supporting strands are vertical and the rope does not stretch. For a steady lift, ignore rope weight, pulley weight, and friction. Then all strands have the same tension, and the pull is G over n. As the load rises by h, the combined change in supporting rope length is n h, so the free end has to move n h.

politics/rights-duties.d94bd3762604: Political rights and freedoms. The rights that let citizens take part in the country’s political life. Voting and standing for election: every citizen aged eighteen or over, whatever their ethnic group, sex, job, family background, religion, education, property or length of residence, except people the law has deprived of political rights. Political freedoms: speech, the press, assembly, association, procession and demonstration. The right to supervise, 监督权: citizens may criticise and make suggestions to any state organ or official, and may report officials who break the law.
politics/rights-duties.d7d8563a060c: Social, economic, cultural and educational rights. The rights that protect a citizen’s living, working and learning. Property: a citizen’s lawful private property may not be violated — you may own, use, benefit from and dispose of it, and inherit. Material help, 物质帮助权: citizens who are old, ill or unable to work have the right to help from the state and society. Work and education belong here too — and they are also duties, see the “both” bar. Citizens are free to do scientific research, create literature and art, and take part in other cultural activities.
politics/rights-duties.2945c08bcd1f: How to defend a right. When a right is harmed, defend it through lawful steps. One, Negotiate, 协商: talk it out directly with the other side. Two, Mediation, 调解: a neutral third party, such as a people’s mediation committee, helps both sides agree. Three, Arbitration, 仲裁: an arbitration body gives a binding decision. Four, Lawsuit, 诉讼: go to court. The textbook calls it the most formal and authoritative way — “the last line of defence”.

politics/state-organs.3cec25ffb063: National Supervisory Commission. Supervisory commissions are the state’s supervisory organs; the National Supervisory Commission is the highest one. Added to the Constitution by the twenty eighteen amendment. It supervises all public employees who exercise public power. Three duties: supervise, investigate, and deal with, 监督, 调查, 处置, duty-related violations and crimes such as bribery. It uses its power independently according to law, free from interference by administrative organs, organisations or individuals.
politics/state-organs.88ecf4558f54: State Council. The State Council, that is, the Central People’s Government, is the executive body of the highest organ of state power and the highest administrative organ. Led by the Premier, 总理, under the “Premier responsibility system”. Runs the country’s administration: the economy, education, science, health, the environment and more. Makes administrative regulations in line with the Constitution and the laws. Local people’s governments are the local administrative organs; all of them are under the State Council’s unified leadership. Governments must act according to law, 依法行政.
politics/state-organs.e6ed85ed7760: Local levels — and the armed forces. The same pattern repeats at each level: province, city, county, township. Each level has a people’s congress and a people’s government. From county level up there are also a supervisory commission, a court and a procuratorate. Each local organ is created by the congress at its own level, answers to it and is supervised by it. The Constitution also sets up the Central Military Commission, 中央军事委员会, which leads the country’s armed forces.
politics/state-organs.112e28a2f3ba: National People’s Congress. The National People’s Congress, NPC, is the highest organ of state power. Legislative power: amends the Constitution; makes and amends basic laws. Power to decide: approves national plans and budgets and other major matters. Power to appoint and remove: elects or decides on the top leaders of the other state organs — and can remove them. Power to supervise: watches over the Constitution and the work of the other organs. Its Standing Committee, 常务委员会, is its permanent body and works when the NPC is not in session. Local people’s congresses are the local organs of state power.
politics/state-organs.8677cb1740db: Watch out: Supervisory, 监察, is not procuratorial, 检察: the commission investigates officials; the procuratorate prosecutes in court.
