yuwen/yw-modern-classics.78493b348301: First published in Tagore’s Bengali collection Shishu in nineteen oh three. Tagore published his own English version in The Crescent Moon in nineteen thirteen. A champa is a fragrant tree blossom.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.64c771174fd9: 无耻啊! An exclamation lets anger be heard in the speaker’s voice, while the neighboring questions demand that people judge what happened.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.004300e7e89d: 不必说……也不必说……单是…… The paired openings sweep across the garden. The turn to a single strip of wall zooms into what a child can hear, touch, and taste.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.95cb07f09f0c: 看风景. Repeated words keep the activity familiar while the viewer and the viewed switch places. That switch is the poem’s main event.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d9f58d3585d1: This Russian lyric was written in eighteen twenty-five and appeared that year in Moscow Telegraph. It takes the form of an intimate address to someone having a difficult time.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.b9b63b4c6877: A memorial poem for Zhou Enlai. It appears in the revised Grade nine, Volume one poetry unit.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1981decf0a5a: 心中的雨点. An image first seen outdoors comes to stand for worry and pain. The plant’s physical shelter suggests a kind of emotional shelter.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6cba8cc9b0b2: Selected prose, stories, and poems from all six national textbook volumes, including international readings. Units follow the revised contents, with notes for supplementary readings from earlier editions. Yin Fu’s poem appears in the Grade nine, Volume two revision preview.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0dbda4c9f77b: Zhu began teaching at Tsinghua in Beijing in nineteen twenty-five, the year the essay appeared. The station in the remembered scene is in Nanjing, across the Yangtze from the city center.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.b10372e4a3cf: 图画美. The phrase sets a test for the design examples. Ask how each example changes what can be seen from a particular viewpoint.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.62171d3a8224: an edible mushroom also written 鸡枞
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.4850fa144d15: Grade nine, Volume two, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.4822fd278a5b: 泛滥. The word often describes water spilling beyond its banks. Applied to feeling, it lets homesickness seem too forceful to contain.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.7bb0e08af07b: A poem from the late nineteen seventies by Shu Ting, associated with the Misty Poets. A chain of objects links hardship, longing, and renewal.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.2d4f568ffa5d: 你在哪里? The recurring question gives a long search a stable rhythm and lets each reply take the reader to a new place.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d219ea592bba: Grade nine, Volume two, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.103756bdafb1: First published in Our Monthly in August nineteen twenty-eight under the name Ren Fu. The poem belongs to the writing of a young poet in Shanghai’s revolutionary literary circles. Listed in the revised Grade nine, Volume two preview.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.8205a1f59bec: The pivot word 却, “yet”, turns a nearby tree into a possible support the speaker does not use. Standing upright can suggest independence in a cold setting.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.dbeb79242617: A Russian prose poem published in the journal Life in April nineteen oh one. It is often read against the social unrest of late imperial Russia. Its central bird flies into a gathering storm.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0278ad82ce5c: zero over eight matched, zero missed
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.192ed946c412: A Russian satirical story first published in the humor magazine Oskolki in eighteen eighty-four. A market dispute repeatedly tests a police officer’s supposed rules.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1460707b8f95: 长夜漫漫. A long night gives duration to grief. The quiet tone leaves the reader room to feel the length rather than hear it explained.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.9a5775c6b9e7: 一枚小小的邮票. The object could fit on a fingertip. What matters is how much distance it must carry. Later objects build on that gap between size and feeling.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.1e5dca78be97: A French short story first printed in Le Gaulois on August seventh, eighteen eighty-three. A family living in Le Havre hopes its fortunes will improve once a relative comes home.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.394a984b9e57: 一滴水. The tiny first-person speaker can move through narrow channels. This choice organizes the entire view of the town from its water system outward.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5b417a7105b4: Xiao Hong knew Lu Xun in Shanghai. She builds his portrait out of encounters and household details. Older textbooks place this excerpt in Grade seven, Volume two, Unit one.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a67f764cb708: First published in nineteen thirty-four in Xuewen. The poem addresses an unnamed “you” through spring imagery. Proposed biographical identifications remain debated.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c553fb5c9866: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit one
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e6b82fa02d25: A short story first published in nineteen seventy-seven. Mountain travelers in southwest China try to find out who maintains a hut that shelters strangers.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.5eae959cff49: 台阶高, 屋主人的地位就相应高. The story makes a social measure literally visible as height. Later details test how much that visible status can change the father’s actual life.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.dda2813453a1: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0aacddbc17a2: 大约孔乙己的确死了. “Probably” registers the limits of the bartender’s knowledge. “Certainly” gives the ending the force of a bleak conclusion about Kong’s injuries and isolation.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.e639c6fb0496: First printed in Fiction Monthly in December nineteen twenty-two and collected in Call to Arms. A grown narrator remembers a rural festival performance in a Jiangnan river village. “I” is the storyteller in a short story.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.81b1a397a472: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit three
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.9a327cae2193: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit four
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d77393e65835: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit five
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.12d45adb819b: Question one of twelve. What do the stories about the hut’s builders and caretakers add in Pear Blossoms by the Mountain Trail?
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f123de1ec9a1: Grade seven, Volume two, Unit six
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.9e091f885153: Chen wrote this group in nineteen thirty-six while facing great danger in the Meiling area. Revised Grade seven places it in Volume one, Unit four. Earlier editions put it in Grade nine, Volume two, Unit one.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.ac76b053f003: Yang Jiang’s first-person essay recalls a Beijing pedicab driver and reconsiders what they meant to each other. It appeared in older Grade seven, Volume two textbooks.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.43a38679e213: 我想念昆明的雨. The recurring sentence frames a collection of apparently loose details. Each remembered object expands what the rain means.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.465b6c78a2b7: 你是. The recurring address makes each scene a new way of naming the same person. Read the quick fragments aloud to hear their light rhythm.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.86b5ba58897f: National textbook platform: Grade seven, Volume two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.21bc078c6697: 力争上游. Language usually applied to people describes the tree’s upward shape. This prepares the shift from physical description to symbolism.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.afcbf2681a65: zero over nine matched, zero missed
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c1739ee5bed7: 吹面不寒. The wind is felt on the skin first. Scent and sound then give it presence even though wind itself is invisible.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.8ed89d6154a1: Zhu De wrote this memorial essay after his mother’s death in nineteen forty-four. Revised textbooks move it to Grade seven, Volume one, Unit four. Earlier books placed it in Grade eight, Volume one, Unit two.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.58c424cced0b: 却没有靠着. The pivot word 却, “yet,” turns a nearby tree into a possible support the speaker does not use. Standing upright can suggest independence in a cold setting.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0eef208e3a20: 神秘的敲击声. The subtitle lets the reader form the same question as the astronaut. A careful account preserves the gap between a sound and its cause.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.acbf2999fbf7: A nineteen twenty-six Mangyuan memoir recollecting the household worker who looked after the young narrator. The illustrated book he wants describes extraordinary places and creatures.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6ca56abd3df7: This lesson gives complete original texts first published by nineteen thirty whose authors died before nineteen seventy-six. Each complete reading credits its edition and notes textbook differences. The reading cards provide our own Chinese and English glosses, and some foreign poems include our own Chinese translations. Dictation follows this lesson’s source editions.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.36c4e179ba3e: 茫茫. A word for enormous, indefinite extent makes it difficult for the young traveler to feel in control. The physical space gives his loneliness an outward form.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a20124a5747c: 双手搂定宝塔山. The embrace is too large to be literal. The imagined movement makes attachment to a place feel as immediate as hugging a person.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.dd04b646c9c1: 两弹元勋. The compact public title is filled out by scenes of private restraint and responsibility. The shifts of scale let readers see both the historical figure and the person.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c3d5eac02c10: 揉过. Giving wind the verb of a hand makes the grass seem touchable. The movement creates intimacy before the poem states any wish to join nature.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d390deb699b8: 万丈绝壁. The huge vertical wall helps the reader judge the movement of a small body and a single cable against the gorge.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.48672763b286: 梨花. The title names both the flowers in the landscape and a person in the story. That echo lets a visible scene carry a memory of care.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.37ed3cabad79: Zhu’s nature essay first appeared in the nineteen thirty-three Junior Chinese Reader.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.23d9a7259a02: 好好儿活. The words change from a mother’s effort to steady her son into something the children can say about how they will live.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6e4e526b30a2: 他用两手攀着上面, 两脚再向上缩. He grabbed the top of the platform with both hands, then pulled his feet up. Hands and feet move in stages. The difficult climb shows how much care went into getting a few oranges. Compare the adult narrator’s ironic description of his younger self as “smart.”
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.a737574139ef: National textbook platform: Grade nine, Volume two, earlier edition
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d5697277becc: Grade eight, Volume one, Unit two
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.c3417ea052f3: 嘶哑的喉咙. An imperfect, strained voice makes the effort to sing audible. The image brings pain and determination together.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.f55b8f526d7a: Chapter four of Keller’s American autobiography, The Story of My Life, published in book form in nineteen oh three. Keller describes learning words through touch as a young deafblind child in Alabama.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.6eb7426a1b1b: 淤滩上的驳船. A heavy workboat stuck in silt makes obstruction imaginable. Later growth images move in the opposite direction.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.0012b51e0af7: 小摇篮. A cradle gently holds a child. Comparing the ring of hills to a cradle makes the city seem sheltered and at ease.
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.d572d78ecc68: Grade eight, Volume one, Unit four
yuwen/yw-modern-classics.3d534f392350: Grade eight, Volume one, Unit five

yuwen/yw-narrative.b7600f4b274d: Counted live by this page from the answer key of Mission three, main method of each sentence. Action leads: narratives show people by what they do.
yuwen/yw-narrative.98db767823a6: Don't mix up: A summary is not copying sentences! Formula: who, in what situation, did what and with what result, usually under forty characters.
yuwen/yw-narrative.7843d735fa2e: Character description comes in five kinds — appearance, 外貌, action, 动作, speech, 语言, thoughts, 心理, and expression, 神态 — plus setting description, 环境. The texts are real: Zhu Ziqing’s “背影”, nineteen twenty-five, and Lu Xun’s “从百草园到三味书屋”, “From Hundred-Plant Garden to Three-Flavour Study”, nineteen twenty-six, both public domain; the third is our own.
yuwen/yw-narrative.653f61d12b49: Notes: excerpts follow the standard texts and were checked against Wikisource. The authors died over seventy years ago, so the texts are in the public domain. “The old umbrella”, “Grandma’s dumplings” and “The exam” are our own passages. Answer templates are common classroom summaries, not textbook wording. English translations are ours.
yuwen/yw-narrative.9bd89a1be439: 人物 — who is in it.
yuwen/yw-narrative.0a80d2a13304: Question one of twelve. Which is NOT one of the six elements of a narrative?
yuwen/yw-narrative.4e40756eef97: Many 中考 reading questions follow a pattern: name the method, say what it describes, then give the effect or feeling. Put the three right pieces into the boxes in order — careful, some pieces only look right.
yuwen/yw-narrative.e4cd2fe4b40d: 起因, 经过, 结果 — why it starts, how it unfolds, how it ends. 经过 is usually the longest part.
yuwen/yw-narrative.8970595e742e: Reading his father’s letter, he sees the back again — the ending echoes the opening, 首尾呼应, and shows deep longing.
yuwen/yw-narrative.9a0eb3b2a185: Same story as Mission one, “The old umbrella”. Switch the order and watch the event cards rearrange.
yuwen/yw-narrative.9140332145eb: third person, 第三人称: the narrator stands outside — free across time and place, more objective, can show several characters.
yuwen/yw-narrative.e40a89ade687: first person, 第一人称: we are inside the narrator’s head — it feels real and close, and feelings can be told directly. But we only know what “I” know.
yuwen/yw-narrative.e6ac1c428953: Every narrative answers six questions: when, 时间, where, 地点, who, 人物, and the event’s cause, 起因, development, 经过, and result, 结果 — like “setting, characters, plot” in US ELA. Pick a label, then tap the matching words. Finish both stories, written for this site, and you can summarise any story.
yuwen/yw-narrative.a92d11aa279e: Textbook, 统编版: “背影” — Grade eight volume one, unit four; “从百草园到三味书屋” — Grade seven volume one, unit three. US link: Georgia K to twelve ELA Standards, grades six to eight — narrative elements, point of view and narrative writing, setting, characters, plot about 六要素.
yuwen/yw-narrative.98d01609e5fe: A clue thread, 线索, is like the string through a pearl necklace: it holds all the material together. In “背影” the thread is the 背影 itself. Open all four appearances and watch the feeling rise.
yuwen/yw-narrative.0a0cd4be7dae: Mission three: label the description methods
yuwen/yw-narrative.79c3ead0d9f5: Lu Xun, nineteen twenty-six, in “朝花夕拾” — public domain
yuwen/yw-narrative.3882319cbc9d: Flashback: creates suspense, hooks the reader. Insertion: fills in background, enriches the character. First person: feels real and personal, easy to express feelings. Third person: free across time and place, more objective.
yuwen/yw-narrative.0403fb2c33e4: Opens with the title word and sets up the whole memory, 开篇点题.
yuwen/yw-narrative.3e0cc8b1bbd9: Zhu Ziqing’s famous essay “背影”, “The Sight of Father’s Back”, nineteen twenty-five, is only about one thousand five hundred characters long — yet the word 背影, “the view of someone’s back”, appears four times. Why write about his father’s back, not his face? Reading a narrative, 记叙文, means spotting the choices the writer made.
yuwen/yw-narrative.198de58ada66: Mission four: build the full-mark 中考 answer
yuwen/yw-narrative.723114166c80: Mission two: follow the clue, switch the order and the narrator
yuwen/yw-narrative.f65389928f44: Your mission: become a story detective — tag the six elements, follow the clue thread, switch the narrator and the order of events, label description methods, and finally build full-mark answers with 中考, the high-school entrance exam, answer templates.
yuwen/yw-narrative.f7943a7299c0: Zhu Ziqing, “背影”, nineteen twenty-five, the orange-buying scene — public domain
yuwen/yw-narrative.1a2602e71e40: 时间 and 地点 — when and where it happens.
yuwen/yw-narrative.bb2348c04ab5: Second person, 第二人称: talks straight to “you” — rare, but it pulls the reader in like a conversation.
yuwen/yw-narrative.a07d475572f2: Twelve questions — nine or more right completes a mission.
yuwen/yw-narrative.7e7326994460: Standard: “义务教育语文课程标准, 二零二二年版”, stage four, grades seven to nine, “reading and appreciation”: read narrative works and understand narration, description, exposition, argument and lyrical expression; task group “literary reading and creative expression”.

yuwen/yw-poems-7.21cf6ece69a4: 寻 was a unit of length. “A thousand xun” makes the tower seem extraordinarily tall.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.b15b8519c4fc: At Qi’s Inn for Breakfast, Passing Songyuan, Number five
yuwen/yw-poems-7.b59d6247051e: 断肠, literally “broken guts,” means heartbreak. 天涯, the edge of the sky, suggests being far from home.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.13b8f8419149: 回乐烽 is a beacon tower in the school reading. 降 in 受降城, Shòuxiáng Chéng, is read xiáng.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.9330bde34d09: 潮平 suggests a full tide widening the visible river. 风正 means the wind blows in the right direction for sailing.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.a1bd0b74032d: 明堂 is a ceremonial hall. 尚书郎 is a government post. “Thousand-li feet” means a swift horse able to go far.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.7ee0478b69f9: 漫漫 suggests a road stretching into the distance. 龙钟 can be read here as tear-soaked.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.06158349d73f: The school text follows the Complete Tang Poems version beginning 客路青山外. The twenty twenty-four revision has a comma after 乡书何处达 where the previous edition had a question mark. The Tang anthology Heyue Yingling Ji preserves Jiangnan Thoughts with readings such as 两岸失 and 数帆悬.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.7e8883670a5a: 折柳 refers to the tune “Breaking a Willow Branch.” 故园 means home.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.764701911e10: The school text uses 杨花落尽 and 随君. The Complete Tang Poems tradition also records 扬州花落 and 随风.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.f64dd4453d4c: 我寄愁心与明月, 随君直到夜郎西. Li Bai entrusts his worries to the moon and asks it to keep his friend company on the journey.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.6eac0efe92b5: Grade seven Volume two, Spring twenty twenty-five release
yuwen/yw-poems-7.730cf111948d: 碣石 is Mount Jieshi. 临 here means to climb to or reach a lookout.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.82d410811657: 弹琴 here means playing the guqin, a string instrument. 长啸 is a long, voiced call or whistle.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.612040d9079d: What does 尽, “all”, contribute to the last line?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.08576da2f719: Question one of two. What detail shows the host passing the time in Waiting for a Guest?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.2f9c60608252: P E P, Notes on the Volume two revision
yuwen/yw-poems-7.03e7858cbfc8: 唧唧 is read here as sighing. 机杼 is a loom and its shuttle, evoking their sound. 军帖 is a call-up notice.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.4b81f8b46d54: 会当 signals a future determination. The mountain’s height inspires the speaker’s spirited ambition to climb it.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.03bd2b87a78e: Volume two, After Unit three, Additional readings
yuwen/yw-poems-7.3ad793c51fe7: How do 生 and 入 show a transition between old and new?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.16f01b2b739d: 吟鞭 is the traveling poet’s riding whip. 落红 means fallen blossoms.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.577e9af96c0d: 己亥 begins with 己, distinct from 已. 浩荡 often describes surging water. Here it describes the sweep of sorrow.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.c9beb0e1579d: 寻常 means “often” here. 闻 leaves its object unstated and refers to hearing Li sing.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.5a8f32f3b4b3: 可汗 is the title “khan.” 爷 means father here. 市 is a verb meaning “buy.” She is willing to buy a mount and gear for the call-up.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.78a65d4939a0: Volume two, Unit two, Ballad of Mulan
yuwen/yw-poems-7.9637f8ff6473: 造化 means nature, and 钟 means to gather. 阴阳 contrast the shaded and sunny sides of the mountain.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.040ddfccfe67: 曾云 are layers of cloud. 决眦 pictures eyes opened wide to look far. 会当 means “I surely will,” and 凌 means to ascend.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.6644f3025dae: 幽篁 is a secluded bamboo grove. 篁 means a stand of bamboo.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.e68da3fae307: The school text uses 错喜欢, 政入 and 围子. A collected version reads 空喜欢, 正入 and 圈子.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.ecfed76066c9: 才调 means talent. 可怜 here means “what a pity.” 前席 shows the emperor shifting closer to Jia Yi on his seat. 虚 marks the gesture as wasted. 苍生 means ordinary people.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.f79b518de523: 怜 is to feel tender concern. 应 signals a guess, and 傍 means beside.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.f1ce7ae4ed9e: Question one of two. What word marks the shift into imagination in Gazing at the Sea?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.5807dc6d5a83: 疑 conveys uncertainty when the winding landscape seems to close in. 又 catches the surprise of encountering a village where the traveler thought the route ended.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.628a732a82ac: What work does the repeated 若 do? Explain using the lines.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.11a6b030c96b: 落花时节 is late spring as blossoms fall. It can also suggest the passing of a splendid era.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.74635097526f: 岱宗 is an honored name for Mount Tai. Qi and Lu were ancient states in what is now Shandong. 未了 means without end.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.ccb8d263dfb2: 春不久归 means spring is about to leave. 斗芳菲 is to compete in fragrance and color.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.813613fd046b: Question one of twelve. What message does the poet ask the messenger to take to his family?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.c1b3fe23ac7d: The school text keeps 曾云, with 曾 read céng, “layer.” Some editions print 層雲 instead.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.bd5290c062e4: 策勋 means to enter military merit in the record. 转 counts ranks and 强 means “and more.” Numbers such as “twelve” and “hundreds or thousands” emphasize scale.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.80c12edce25d: 宣室 is a Han palace chamber. 访 is to consult. 逐臣 is an official sent into exile or demoted away from court.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.69d50eee862f: Volume two, After Unit six, Additional readings
yuwen/yw-poems-7.ddbc3d5fbc24: 排云 means to push through the clouds. 碧霄 is the blue sky above. The character is 霄.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.cc9e489cb5b9: What state of mind does each of 疑 and 又 suggest in the second couplet?
yuwen/yw-poems-7.59a15841da4d: 玉笛 is a graceful name for a flute. 暗飞声 suggests sound drifting from an unseen source.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.dfb4fb73f89c: 灯花 is a flowerlike crust on a burned oil-lamp wick. 闲敲 is idly tapping.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.8482e6a328bd: The school text uses 丛生, “grow thickly”. The collected text records 聚生 as a variant.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.0bff3dde7877: 潼关 is the name of a historic pass. 终古 means since ages past, and 簇 means to cluster around.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.53b4d589d6d4: 泊 means to moor a boat. 笼 is to cover or veil. 烟 here suggests mist over the water.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.98859a6db1fa: 鞍鞯 means saddle and pad. 辔头 means bridle and reins. 溅溅 imitates rushing water, while 啾啾 here imitates horses.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.e9ee4142a4cb: 山重 means hills layered one behind another. 柳暗 is the deep shade of willows, set against bright flowers.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.be0213c92534: Volume two, Unit five, Five classical poems
yuwen/yw-poems-7.9f9afc242294: 望眼 is the far-reaching gaze. 自缘 means “because” here.
yuwen/yw-poems-7.13f36d036482: Question one of two. What did the speaker hear “several times” in Meeting Li Guinian?

yuwen/yw-poems-9.cc9e9612b6f6: Late Tang poet Li Shangyin left several poems labeled “Untitled.” This one gives no named lovers or occasion, and can be read as a poem of longing across separation. Silk and wax give lasting longing a material form, and 思 hides in the sound of 丝. “方” and “始” delay the end. The imagined messenger makes the poem turn from solitary feeling toward a possible connection.

yuwen/yw-poems-9.f3c2e71325a3: Tang poet Liu Changqing visited the former home of Jia Yi, a Han scholar-official demoted to Changsha. Liu’s own demotions give the visit personal weight. yuwen/yw-poems-9.e203f019407b: Su Shi was living in exile in Huangzhou in ten eighty-two. A shower on the road to Shahu, described in his preface, gives him the setting for thinking about how to weather setbacks. The verbs “chant” and “walk slowly” tell us how he handles the downpour. The last line looks back from the same walk and levels rain and sunshine into two experiences he can accept.

yuwen/yw-poems-9.b8fb95de8529: In autumn seven hundred fifty-nine Du Fu was staying in Qinzhou. The An Lushan Rebellion had scattered his family and disrupted contact with his brothers. One goose call stands out against the empty road. Calling the hometown moon brighter makes the landscape personal. The stalled letters locate homesickness in the practical danger of war.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.f014a40b70f2: Su Shi was living in exile in Huangzhou in ten eighty-two. A shower on the road to Shahu, described in his preface, gives him the setting for thinking about how to weather setbacks.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.8cfefbbf5a0d: Yuan writer Zhang Yanghao looks from Mount Li near modern Xi’an across a landscape associated with Qin. “One blaze at Epang” draws on a literary tradition. Excavation of the palace’s front hall site found no evidence of that fire. An extravagant palace gives way to grass, water and mist. “赢” and “输” receive exactly the same answer, putting the pursuit of power against its long-term results.

yuwen/yw-poems-9.3c674044cda0: Rain on clothes is immediate. Against it, “千古” and “一时” set long-lasting land beside abruptly changed rule. The wild greens turn private grief into a declaration of allegiance.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.ee168ecccda0: prestige; what is real and what is fake, with 共 meaning “and”
yuwen/yw-poems-9.bd77325d18b6: Xia Wanchun joined Ming loyalist resistance during the dynastic transition. In sixteen forty-seven he was captured and later executed at Nanjing. Yunjian is an old name for his home district, Songjiang.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.5d2c67aaec2f: In eight hundred nineteen Han Yu protested the emperor’s reception of a Buddhist relic. He was sent to a post in distant Chaozhou, and addressed his grandnephew Han Xiang on the journey. Morning and evening squeeze the punishment into a single day and “eight thousand li” stretches the road ahead. Clouds cut off the look back while snow blocks the way forward, giving his conviction a lonely setting.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.7e5ac7404b2c: Some historical texts print 廖落 or 風拋絮. The textbook uses 寥落 and 风飘絮. The waters are also called 伶仃洋.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.cb7efe6a1490: Nalan Xingde was a Manchu lyricist and Qing court guard whose duties took him outside the capital. The speaker here crosses a northern frontier landscape in late autumn. Wind interrupts the sound just as the eye finds a wisp of smoke and a low sun. The sparse details make the frontier feel empty. “古今” stretches a solitary journey across many people’s memories.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.c0a17507ff9d: silk sounds like 思, longing; wax candle

yuwen/yw-poems-9.b12319815c83: Du Fu. Stayed in Qinzhou, modern Tianshui, Gansu, during the An Lushan Rebellion. 月夜忆舍弟, Thinking of My Brothers on a Moonlit Night

yuwen/yw-poems-9.d8adb67568da: Captured by Yuan forces, Wen Tianxiang was escorted north through Nan’an, near present-day Dayu in Jiangxi. The road brought him nearer his home region as a prisoner. Rain on clothes is immediate. Against it, “千古” and “一时” set long-lasting land beside abruptly changed rule. The wild greens turn private grief into a declaration of allegiance.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.b504e84af623: Question one of two. In Chen Yuyi’s Linjiangxian, which pairing marks the move from memory to the present?
yuwen/yw-poems-9.14aac36f8efd: The textbook also notes the title 咸阳城西楼晚眺. The Complete Tang Poems records 前朝 in place of 当年, and 渭水寒声昼夜流 as an alternate last line. Dictation uses 当年 and 故国东来渭水流.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.7fc606a607dd: The Yuan army captured Southern Song official Wen Tianxiang in twelve seventy-eight. The following year, as he passed through Lingding Waters at the Pearl River estuary, he wrote this declaration of loyalty under captivity.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.8be88f4dbad8: The mismatch between a tiny tune and a huge sound ridicules inflated status. In the repeated verb “吹,” making noise turns into harming households. The impossible power of the horn points to the officials behind it.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.af974401b2db: 忽如一夜春风来, 千树万树梨花开. As though a spring wind had come overnight, pear blossoms opened on thousands upon thousands of trees. Cen Shen

yuwen/yw-poems-9.505a23bd4d27: Han Yu. Appointed to Chaozhou, now in Guangdong, after his memorial angered the emperor. 左迁至蓝关示侄孙湘, At Blue Pass, to My Grandnephew Xiang, After Demotion
yuwen/yw-poems-9.3f82bfb82b5e: What does the contrast between 身 and 心 reveal?
yuwen/yw-poems-9.55745cc4309a: The textbook joins “赢, 都变做了土” and “输, 都变做了土” with a semicolon. Some editions print these as separate verse lines.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.671c07e843fc: Some editions pause after 早又是, 为篱下 and 苦将侬. The textbook runs those words into the clauses that follow.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.d5c00661fc79: The textbook has 已而遂晴 and 竹杖. Some witnesses omit 遂 or write 拄杖.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.d825abbff9ee: The textbook prints 饴阿谁. Many yuefu witnesses read 贻阿谁; the sense is “give to whom?”
yuwen/yw-poems-9.8450ce05e3b5: The textbook uses 楚客 and 独寻. The Complete Tang Poems also records 楚国 and 渐寻.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.1d8595ea5b93: The textbook reads 枳花明驿墙. Some received texts use 照 in place of 明.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.93f597bc5ae4: In autumn seven fifty-nine Du Fu was staying in Qinzhou. The An Lushan Rebellion had scattered his family and disrupted contact with his brothers.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.bb17a519e23a: 长沙过贾谊宅, Passing Jia Yi’s House in Changsha
yuwen/yw-poems-9.e167e1f4baa6: Late Qing revolutionary Qiu Jin wrote in Beijing at Mid-Autumn in nineteen oh three. She challenged the roles imposed on women and later studied in Japan. The short, balanced phrases put social status and inward resolve face to face. The Chu allusion makes constraint feel like a siege. Bai Juyi’s wet robe then gives the loneliness of finding few allies a visible sign.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.f329bc4c8ef3: 南乡子, 登京口北固亭有怀, Nanxiangzi, Reflections from Beigu Pavilion at Jingkou
yuwen/yw-poems-9.628617b8277b: Su Shi wrote this while governing Mizhou. The organized hunt becomes the occasion for imagining military service on the Song frontier. “卷” packs the speed and scale of the hunt into one verb. The Sun Quan allusion shapes the hunter’s public image, and Feng Tang’s mission turns the hunt into a plea for a real assignment. The final bow image gives that wish a direction.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.44268a7a58a6: Wind interrupts the sound just as the eye finds a wisp of smoke and a low sun. The sparse details make the frontier feel empty. “古今” stretches a solitary journey across many people’s memories.

yuwen/yw-poems-9.cd83f4bcf40f: 满江红, 小住京华, Manjianghong, A Short Stay in the Capital
yuwen/yw-poems-9.82a35722b836: The textbook reads 归乡如此归. The Sibu Congkan edition of Wen Tianxiang’s collection reads 归乡如不归.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.e8c2907e3d2b: Cen Shen. Served on the northwestern frontier, including at the Tang headquarters at Beiting, modern Jimsar, Xinjiang. 白雪歌送武判官归京, Song of White Snow, Seeing Adjutant Wu Off to the Capital
yuwen/yw-poems-9.2bb1739f8c80: 浣溪沙, 身向云山那畔行, Huanxisha, Riding Toward the Cloud-Wrapped Mountains

yuwen/yw-poems-9.9ef911d9d234: Silk, 丝, sounds like longing, 思, so the thread is also a feeling. The candle’s tears turn the same persistence into an image of grief. Both last until their source is spent.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.98f3b35a07a9: The textbook prints 珍羞 and 直. The collected editions also record 清 versus 美 and 碧溪 versus 坐溪. Use the form shown in the main text for dictation.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.981c6b609381: Xia Wanchun joined Ming loyalist resistance during the dynastic transition. In sixteen forty-seven he was captured and later executed at Nanjing. Yunjian is an old name for his home district, Songjiang. “天地宽” is challenged by someone with no room to act. The last couplet imagines a spirit that can return even when the body cannot. The battle flag gives grief a continuing purpose.
yuwen/yw-poems-9.a1c11554f295: right before one’s eyes; blowing until, where 的 functions like 得

yuwen/yw-poems-9.5d56ef003176: Silk and wax give lasting longing a material form, and 思 hides in the sound of 丝. “方” and “始” delay the end. The imagined messenger makes the poem turn from solitary feeling toward a possible connection.

yuwen/yw-rhetoric.dc28a171de81: Describe one thing, A, by naming a different thing, B, that is like it. Simile: A 像 B. Metaphor: A 是 B. Sometimes only B appears.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.110ee59e50c9: one quarter, Find the line with PERSONIFICATION, 拟人.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.4cf19f9d62eb: Count the matching parts: three or more
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.e4ae11fe9783: Exam answers: thirteen of sixteen points
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.3371662b9036: Humble Room. Today: He County, Anhui. Tradition says Liu Yuxi wrote “陋室铭” while governor of Hezhou, where the town gave him only a tiny room. A rebuilt “humble room” stands in He County today.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.3c6de77aca9e: 陋室铭, “An Inscription on My Humble Room”, Liu Yuxi, Tang dynasty, has only eighty-one characters but packs in several devices. Find the line the prompt asks for; after four finds you unlock the lenses to see them all.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.865ea1655a8c: Don't mix up: Only two matching parts? Not parallelism — it needs at least three. Two equal lines may be antithesis, 对偶.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.327dc9c3634a: Don't mix up: 设问 has the answer right after it. 反问 has no answer after it — the answer hides inside the question.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.774eb93e2f09: Exam template: Uses hypophora, asks, then answers, catching the reader’s attention and making them think; leads into …运用设问的修辞手法, 自问自答, 引起读者的注意和思考, 结构上, 引出下文……
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.ed9520b87e33: Old Drunkard’s Pavilion. Today: Mount Langya, Chuzhou, Anhui. The monk Zhixian built it and Ouyang Xiu named it after himself. With its wing-like roof corners, 翼然, it is one of China’s four famous pavilions.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.9201c52df7c9: Memory hook: 排 equals line up, 比 equals side by side: three or more in a row, like soldiers.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.8ffd8b206376: Impossible numbers or sizes: 三千尺, 三千丈
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.dec4f4a8f2ac: Parallelism: three or more parts, lengths may differ. Antithesis: exactly two lines of equal length.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.1911a65e0529: Textbook links, 统编版: 春 and 济南的冬天, Grade seven volume one, unit one, 从百草园到三味书屋, Grade seven volume one, unit three, 木兰诗, Grade seven volume two, unit two, 陋室铭 and 爱莲说, Grade seven volume two, unit four, 岳阳楼记 and 醉翁亭记, Grade nine volume one, unit three.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.3dffb45c80fd: Devices in 陋室铭, eighty-one characters, eight lines
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.a659ef75a5f5: Exam template: Uses a rhetorical question, strengthening the tone and stressing …运用反问的修辞手法, 加强了语气, 强调了……, 表达了……
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.8d8f84bd304b: Uses a simile or metaphor, comparing A to B; vividly shows feature; expresses feeling.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.09e8c44f9c4c: Is there a picture B, 像 something? Simile. Does the thing just act like a person? Personification.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.39665d2bf7f4: Memory hook: Three parts: the thing, 本体, the “like” word, 喻词, the picture, 喻体. A and B must be DIFFERENT kinds of things that share a feature.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.6ea60f00c9a0: Your mission: meet the eight devices Chinese exams love, become a rhetoric detective, upgrade plain sentences, and learn the exam formula for explaining what a device does.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.6758972ece7c: Notes: classical texts are public domain; modern works, for example Zhu Ziqing’s 春, are quoted one sentence at a time. “Example sentences” are written for this page. The 陋室铭 chart follows this page’s tagging, a line with two devices counts for both; study guides may differ slightly. The answer templates are common classroom summaries, not the only correct wording.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.4356d23426e0: Uses personification, giving thing human actions or feelings; vividly shows …; expresses …
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.5f741053482e: 设问, Hypophora, ask, then answer
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.29e9c3c8d497: Don't mix up: One sentence can use several devices at once: 苔痕上阶绿, 草色入帘青 is antithesis AND personification, the moss “climbs”, the grass “comes in”. 孔子云: 何陋之有? is a quotation AND a rhetorical question. In an exam, answer the device the question asks about.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.f43980002025: Don't mix up: Hyperbole must be obviously not literal — nobody thinks the waterfall is exactly three thousand chi. A real measurement is not hyperbole.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.e8b16c53039f: Don't mix up: Test: turn it into a plain statement. 何陋之有, “It is not shabby at all.”
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.449df1dea474: Don't mix up: 花儿笑了 equals personification, the flower does a human action. 花儿像一张张笑脸 equals simile, it is compared to a face.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.63e541bb51fc: Turn a plain sentence into a vivid one: choose a device, then pick the best of four fillers. A good simile must be alike in a way that makes sense; personification must fit the mood; parallelism needs three parts. Best choice equals three points; five best upgrades complete the mission.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.ed28bc1fe0e3: Standard: 义务教育语文课程标准, 二零二二年版, stage four: appreciate the effect of common rhetorical devices while reading; the appendix on grammar and rhetoric lists 比喻, 拟人, 夸张, 排比, 对偶, 反复, 设问, 反问, 引用, quotation, is a common classroom addition; 反复, repetition, is not covered here.

yuwen/yw-rhetoric.e975a6c49772: Don't mix up: Spring Festival couplets, 对联, are antithesis! But two lines of different lengths are not.

yuwen/yw-rhetoric.523a59bd4e03: Yellow Crane Tower. Today: Snake Hill, Wuchang, Wuhan. A tower on Snake Hill above the Yangtze, first built about one thousand eight hundred years ago. Legend says an immortal flew away from it on a yellow crane.
yuwen/yw-rhetoric.3fcb75ead542: US link: the Georgia K to twelve ELA Standards for grades six to eight ask students to interpret figurative language — simile, metaphor, personification, hyperbole — the same skills, so the English names are given throughout. yuwen/yw-rhetoric.df5cd106a8ae: two quarters, Find the line with a QUOTATION, 引用.

yuwen/yw-rhetoric.22e56e21d473: Jinan. Jinan has more than seventy famous springs; the water of Baotu Spring bubbles up all year round.

yuwen/yw-song-ci.e7a29d4a4234: Key words: 鹏 equals the giant roc from Zhuangzi, flying ninety thousand li. 三山 equals the three islands of the immortals.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.83fa8336a7d7: Yanzhou. Today: Yan’an, Shaanxi. A Song fortress city on the Loess Plateau facing the Western Xia. Fan Zhongyan’s “渔家傲, 秋思” shows the soldiers’ lonely autumn here.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.325e0910c437: Guess three ci tunes from their boxes
yuwen/yw-song-ci.aa15909ce973: Don't mix up: The tune is not the topic. Fan Zhongyan and Li Qingzhao both wrote to 渔家傲 — one about a cold frontier, the other about a dream voyage across the sky.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.1b193dadf978: Two styles are often named: bold and unrestrained, 豪放: Su Shi, Xin Qiji, and delicate and graceful, 婉约: Liu Yong, Li Qingzhao.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.3dec85f98d2e: Background: Li Qingzhao is famous for graceful ci, but this dream voyage is bold and soaring. Li Qingzhao lived from ten eighty-four to about eleven fifty-five.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.3a72a86f634e: The tune name, 词牌, fixes the number of characters, line lengths, tones and rhymes. A topic title may follow it: 渔家傲, 秋思 equals tune “The Fisherman’s Pride”, topic “Autumn Thoughts”.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.afe5cd46eda3: Most ci have two stanzas, 双调: 上阕, upper, and 下阕, lower.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.30f68794bed0: Mount Yanran. Today: the Khangai Mountains, Mongolia. In eighty-nine C E the Han general Dou Xian beat the Xiongnu and carved a record of victory on a cliff — 勒石燕然. Archaeologists found that inscription in Mongolia in twenty seventeen.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.e9a53af6e379: Standard: 义务教育语文课程标准, 二零二二年版, stage four “Reading and appreciation”: recite classical poems; understand the basic features of literary forms. All ci here are textbook texts or on the recommended recitation list.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.7d57dee31a0a: Background: Fan Zhongyan commanded the northwest frontier against Western Xia around ten forty, based at Yanzhou, today’s Yan’an, Shaanxi.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.12240cbb9746: Theme. 中考 answer: The joy and freedom of youth, in light, fresh language.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.e2acb47d5c23: Modern tone four, guess: oblique. Classical: oblique, 仄.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.e5435cb9796a: Counted from the texts, 满江红: Yue Fei’s; 念奴娇: Su Shi’s “Red Cliff”. The Qing-dynasty Imperial Ci Register, 钦定词谱, lists eight hundred twenty-six tunes in two thousand three hundred six variants; the Complete Song Ci, 全宋词, holds about twenty thousand ci.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.a1afe482ff6f: Personal feelings and small moments in light, flowing language — Li Qingzhao rowing into the lotus flowers. But her 渔家傲 is bold and soaring: style labels are only a guide.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.9f04fec67217: Luoyang. Thirteen dynasties made Luoyang their capital. Near the city, the Longmen Grottoes hold about one hundred thousand Buddhist statues carved into the cliffs.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.23d0447ec978: Modern tone four, guess: oblique. Classical: oblique, 仄, an entering-tone, 入声, character.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.8f7d1f6247a3: Theme. 中考 answer: The bleak frontier autumn; soldiers torn between homesickness and the duty to win first, 燕然未勒.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.d9a3db6775c8: Key words: 燕然未勒: in eighty-nine C E the Han general Dou Xian carved a victory record on Mount Yanran — the war isn’t won yet. 衡阳: geese were said to stop at Huiyan Peak in Hengyang.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.97e508e4c967: Modern tone two, guess: level. Classical: level, 平.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.9d4fd6091f78: Question one of twelve. What does 婵娟 mean in “千里共婵娟”?
yuwen/yw-song-ci.cd37dcf2c20d: Su Causeway. Today: West Lake, Hangzhou. Su Shi dug the weeds and mud out of West Lake and piled them into this two point eight kilometer causeway with six bridges. “Spring dawn on the Su Causeway” is one of the lake’s Ten Views.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.2b7cfee80925: Background: ten seventy-five, Mizhou, today’s Zhucheng, Shandong: Su Shi, about forty, led a hunt. Northwest lay the rival states of Liao and Western Xia.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.16e1e3055611: Blue equals level tone, 平, orange equals oblique tone, 仄. Press “Guess from modern tones”: tones one to two count as level, three to four as oblique — but some characters come out wrong! Most are old “entering-tone” characters, 入声, a short clipped sound Mandarin has lost. Tap every character the modern guess gets wrong.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.88fc28006c82: 丙辰中秋, 欢饮达旦, 大醉, 作此篇, 兼怀子由. Mid-Autumn Festival, ten seventy-six: I drank happily till dawn, got very drunk, and wrote this — also thinking of Ziyou, my younger brother Su Zhe.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.b0f10add35bd: Notes: tones follow the traditional Pingshui rhyme tables, for example 国, 白, 别, 达, 一 are entering-tone equals oblique; 胜 in 春望 is level. Pinyin shows modern Mandarin. English versions are our own. Tune lengths are counted from the ci on this page. US link: compare stress and rhyme patterns in English verse, Georgia ELA, poetic structure and sound devices.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.ef3b93123199: Theme 中考 answer: Missing his brother; from frustration to an open, optimistic view of life, 旷达.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.886e5641f3b2: Old Chinese had four tones: level, 平, rising, 上, departing, 去, and entering, 入. Poets grouped the last three as “oblique”, 仄. Regulated verse alternates them like a drumbeat.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.b4482243f07c: Dongpo Red Cliff, Huangzhou. Today: Huanggang, Hubei. Su Shi wrote “念奴娇, 赤壁怀古”, the two Red Cliff rhapsodies and “记承天寺夜游” here. This is not the battlefield of two hundred eight, that is in today’s Chibi City, upstream — Su Shi himself wrote “人道是”, people say…
yuwen/yw-song-ci.f4d25a475553: Rhymes 前 悬 年 边 still rhyme today, ián or uán. Traps: 一, yī, and 达, dá, look level in Mandarin, but were entering tones.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.73e0b449a12f: Key words: 八百里 equals the name of a famous ox, roast beef for the troops. 的卢 equals Liu Bei’s legendary fast horse.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.c65009c1e714: Mission three: read the ci — rhyme detective
yuwen/yw-song-ci.bb542f8b6f0e: Your mission: open up the “boxes” of a ci tune, hear the rise and fall of level and oblique tones, 平仄, catch every rhyme, and get to know Su Shi, Fan Zhongyan, Li Qingzhao and Xin Qiji.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.3176e3150a16: Theme 中考 answer: Through a dream journey she expresses dissatisfaction with reality and a longing for freedom and a better world.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.f4229a0a6ebf: Key words: 婵娟 equals the moon, literally “a lovely lady”. 不胜寒 equals unable to bear the cold.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.7126ef511627: Background: Xin Qiji fought the Jin invaders as a young man but the Southern Song court rarely let him lead. Xin Qiji lived from eleven forty to twelve oh seven. 陈同甫 is his friend Chen Liang.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.6a0e40917790: Don't mix up: Modern tones one and two are mostly level, three and four oblique — except entering-tone characters like 国, 白, 一, 达, which were short and clipped and always oblique.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.4183402fb8cb: Mission one: ci tunes — each tune is a set of boxes
yuwen/yw-song-ci.6d703d29b73d: Ci began in the Sui-Tang era and flowered in the Song, nine hundred sixty to twelve seventy-nine. They were song lyrics, sung to music — hence 曲子词, “song words”.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.bd6fb24284e5: Background: Written in ten seventy-six at Mizhou, today’s Zhucheng, Shandong. Su Shi had not seen his brother Su Zhe for about seven years.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.769a1d0d46e1: Yunzhong. Today: around Togtoh, Inner Mongolia. The general Wei Shang guarded Yunzhong against the Xiongnu; the emperor sent Feng Tang to pardon him. Su Shi’s “持节云中” hopes the court will call him back the same way.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.3ee9788ba0fc: Modern tone one, guess: level. Classical: level, 平.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.4ea0f9b4fdd3: Mizhou. Today: Zhucheng, Shandong. Here Su Shi led the hunt of “江城子, 密州出猎”, ten seventy-five, and, on the Chaoran Terrace he rebuilt, wrote “水调歌头” for his brother at Mid-Autumn ten seventy-six.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.b4d3d38b4d53: Key words: 冯唐: a Han official sent to pardon a general — Su Shi hopes to be “pardoned” and used again. 天狼 equals Sirius, standing for invaders from the northwest.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.25285d3ec0e9: Theme 中考 answer: Bold hunting scene; his wish to be used by the court and defend the frontier.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.f43a673c5138: Theme 中考 answer: A dream of glorious battle — and the grief of growing old with his ambition unfulfilled, 壮志难酬.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.a7f0e4095df0: Key words: Single stanza, 单调, only thirty-three characters. 争渡 equals “row hard, hurry across”.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.a07d475572f2: Twelve questions — nine or more right completes a mission.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.b9e69df341e1: Modern tone three, guess: oblique. Classical: oblique, 仄.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.6941b3c1861e: Pick a tune. Each square is one character; orange squares are rhymes. Ci lines are long and short — that’s why ci are also called 长短句, “long-and-short lines”. A regulated poem, 律诗, has the same number of characters in every line.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.2ff33df74440: Memory hook: “一三五不论, 二四六分明” — in a line, the first, third, fifth characters are free; the second, fourth, and sixth must follow the pattern.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.736983be1b45: Mission two: see the tones and the rhymes
yuwen/yw-song-ci.72b988bdddeb: A 律诗 always has eight lines of five or seven characters. A ci tune lets lines be two, three, four, five, six or seven characters long.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.8f1a25790b7d: “Shui Diao Ge Tou” isn’t the title of Su Shi’s moon poem — it’s the name of a tune. Song-dynasty poets “filled in words”, 填词, to existing melodies, a bit like writing new lyrics to a song you know. Each tune fixes how long every line is and where the rhymes fall.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.93cfc273d5eb: Rhymes 深 心 金 簪 all belonged to one old rhyme group — but in Mandarin 簪, zān, no longer sounds like shēn, xīn, jīn! 胜 here means “bear, stand” and was read in the level tone, shēng.
yuwen/yw-song-ci.1285a0a4d830: Zhangqiu, Jinan. Today: Zhangqiu District, Jinan, Shandong. Li Qingzhao, the greatest woman poet of the Song, grew up here among springs, streams and lotus ponds — like the lotus flowers she rowed into in “如梦令”.

yuwen/yw-tang-poems.6151794a01e6: Standard: 义务教育语文课程标准, 二零二二年版, stage four “Reading and appreciation”: recite classical poems and build taste through accumulation and use; task group “Literary reading and creative expression”. All seven poems are on the standard’s recommended recitation list.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.d15c9cc3f32d: Theme 中考 answer: Wide, bright river scenery; homesickness; and a hint that the new grows out of the old.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.639abbb579b3: Like a painting: the straight smoke is a vertical line, the river a horizontal line, the sun a circle. Two adjectives — 直 and 圆 — do all the work.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.4d437d2cc86a: the Sage of Poetry, 诗圣
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.d97db5278455: How to appreciate it, 次北固山下
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.18a34e3a3929: Sort them all to complete Mission three.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.30f68794bed0: Mount Yanran. Today: the Khangai Mountains, Mongolia. In eighty-nine C E the Han general Dou Xian beat the Xiongnu and carved a record of victory on a cliff — 勒石燕然. Archaeologists found that inscription in Mongolia in twenty seventeen.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.99fcdd33f9b7: Background: Written by the young Du Fu around seven hundred thirty-six, after failing the imperial exam — he still felt the world was his. Du Fu was about twenty-four.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.a16081f7e5c2: Mission one: step into the picture
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.9f18d5f75b31: The first four lines break the usual tone rules, 黄鹤 three times, yet the poem is called the best Tang seven-character regulated verse. Moves from legend, real view, homesickness.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.1b85a59e09bd: Twelve questions, including “which line fits?” recall items. Nine or more right completes Mission four.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.dc81081b5cfd: Personification of the moon, 拟人, turns worry into something you can send — a famous, gentle way to comfort a friend.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.24d3b3647d82: Theme 中考 answer: Paints the vast, grand frontier; a hint of loneliness and drifting, and admiration for the soldiers.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.ab0b6e12d853: Theme 中考 answer: Joy and love for West Lake in early spring, 早春.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.9f04fec67217: Luoyang. Thirteen dynasties made Luoyang their capital. Near the city, the Longmen Grottoes hold about one hundred thousand Buddhist statues carved into the cliffs.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.652087d9c40b: Mount Tai. Mount Tai in Shandong is one thousand five hundred forty-five meters high. Emperors climbed it to honour Heaven, and Du Fu dreamed of standing on its summit: “一览众山小”.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.8391f0d4713f: A realist poet whose works recorded the An Lushan Rebellion, seven hundred fifty-five to seven hundred sixty-three, so they are called “history in verse”. Young Du Fu wrote the confident Gazing at Mount Tai; the older Du Fu wrote the sorrowful Spring View.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.59c2bbc03eb5: the Immortal of Poetry, 诗仙
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.068a9f6a9bc7: Eight lines per round. Step one: tap the image in the line, one character of it is enough. Step two: decide what feeling it carries. Finding the image equals five points; the right feeling equals ten points.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.ffadb418a066: the Buddha of Poetry, 诗佛
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.ef9ad66501c4: Click fifteen images in the pictures
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.c7b937ff5d6e: How to appreciate it, 钱塘湖春行
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.7c8c86a7d25e: Look for the clue word: 早, early orioles, 新, new swallows, 渐欲, starting to, 才能, just enough — all show EARLY spring.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.71c4bc88bfea: Personification, 拟人: the moon becomes a messenger who carries Li Bai’s worry to his friend. Both of them can see it.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.07f27cb7ff28: the Ghost of Poetry, 诗鬼
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.df794b32df69: Structure: far view, lines one to two. Close view, three to four. Fine detail, five to six. Imagined summit, seven to eight. The poem never says “I climbed” — it is all gazing, 望.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.be431f05476e: How to appreciate it, 望岳
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.2c44f64ff4c9: 杨花落尽子规啼, 闻道龙标过五溪. The willow catkins have all fallen and the cuckoo cries; I hear you must cross the Five Streams to Longbiao.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.b1386f7e2d39: 柳, liǔ, sounds like 留, liú, “stay”, so friends gave willow twigs when parting.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.93592c6b5803: How to appreciate it, 使至塞上
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.24dd9da4f18e: Background: Wang Wan, from Luoyang, was travelling on the Yangtze near Beigu Mountain, Zhenjiang, Jiangsu, at the turn of the year. 次 means “to stop over”.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.f028acf480e9: The cuckoo’s cry was said to sound like “better go home”, 不如归去 — a sound of sorrow.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.88dda48bba49: Theme 中考 answer: The grandeur of Mount Tai, and the poet’s ambition to reach the top in life and never fear difficulty.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.080fe31e163b: How to appreciate it, 黄鹤楼
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.b9fbeac37d23: Approximate counts of surviving poems as usually cited from the Qing-dynasty Complete Tang Poems, 全唐诗, seventeen oh five. Cui Hao has only about forty poems — and one of them made him famous for ever.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.04b96506b006: Background: Bai Juyi was governor of Hangzhou, eight hundred twenty-two to eight hundred twenty-four. Qiantang Lake is today’s West Lake, 西湖; the white sand dyke is today’s Bai Causeway, 白堤.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.389ae247ec4d: 我寄愁心与明月, 随君直到夜郎西. I send my worried heart to the bright moon, to follow you all the way west of Yelang.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.bd80a75af31b: Theme 中考 answer: From a legend to the real view, ending in homesickness at dusk, 怀古思乡.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.130ae9a14295: Question one of twelve. Du Fu is honoured as…
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.03c64cdc68fa: Key technique: 借景抒情, using scenery to express feeling, and 以乐景写哀情 — lovely spring things, flowers, birds, make the sadness sharper.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.f32a84a69d80: Read aloud three poems to the end
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.b59ce1802d88: Theme 中考 answer: Sympathy and concern for a friend sent far away.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.dc7a3cb69048: Juyan. Today: Ejin Banner, Inner Mongolia. An oasis at the end of the Heihe River, in the desert far to the northwest. Han soldiers guarded it, and more than ten thousand of their wooden writing slips have been dug up here.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.6f5d67ba13c8: How many poems survive? Complete Tang Poems: about forty-eight thousand nine hundred poems by two thousand two hundred or more poets
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.b5a44a0b7ae4: How to appreciate it, 春望
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.03fe9e274c5e: Background: Li Bai’s friend, the poet Wang Changling, was demoted, 左迁, to a remote post at Longbiao, today’s Hongjiang, Hunan.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.07ae02d2ef0e: The secret is the 意象, “image”: a thing in the scene — the moon, a wild goose, a willow — that carries a feeling. Your mission: step into seven textbook poems, click the images in each picture, listen and read along, then hunt images in the game.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.7be85ba2a292: Image hunter: six or more feelings right
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.039a1f683803: Qi and Lu. Today: Shandong. Qi lay north of Mount Tai and Lu, Confucius’s home state, to the south. Even today Shandong is called 齐鲁 for short.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.76fdbbf8094f: Theme 中考 answer: Grief for the war-torn country and longing for his family, 感时伤乱, 忧国思家.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.4a879b0b948c: Background: Spring seven hundred fifty-seven: during the An Lushan Rebellion, Du Fu was trapped in rebel-held Chang’an, today’s Xi’an, cut off from his family.
yuwen/yw-tang-poems.bdd6b78a24c9: Background: In seven hundred thirty-seven the emperor sent Wang Wei to the northwest frontier to congratulate the army on a victory — partly a way to move him out of the capital.

yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.ccb18315bce0: 不若燔土, 用讫再火令药镕. The comparison of wood and clay explains the material choice based on evenness and easy removal. The interest lies in practical effects the reader can picture.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.db76688a0d58: Unit three. Twelve Passages from the Analects
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.47b462c3ded5: The binder starts to melt. Level like a whetstone.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.143db5728968: Place little value on fame and gain. Have no means to do something.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.d7806ddd1593: 有 links the ten and the five. 逾矩 means “step beyond the rules.”
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.94e990753a73: 徐以杓酌油沥之, 自钱孔入, 而钱不湿. The steady pour through the coin’s opening and the dry rim make skill visible. The result gives the argument its force.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.f91e58b862af: Feet twitching, eyes half closed, running close to the ground. The rabbits are part of the poem’s playful comparison.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.5a1701bd2e55: 逝者如斯夫, 不舍昼夜. The river gives an image to the abstract feeling of time passing beyond recall.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.25b58c4f46f0: Reply. The labor freed when one person no longer has to fetch water.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.96cb5c106268: Set down the shoulder load. Glance sidelong, suggesting little awe.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.38067f265cd5: This reading follows the older textbook. 木杮 contains 杮, fèi, wood shaving; it resembles 柿, shì, persimmon. Editions may spell the character for scour as 齧 instead of 啮.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.7a9975834039: 卿 is how Sun addresses his subordinate. 孤 is a ruler’s way of saying “I.”
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.72f19d33dbcd: An era name of the Northern Song emperor Renzong. A commoner.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.9d6db8c098b6: Dig a well. 穿 means dig through here.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.62e1febe30de: 莲之爱, 同予者何人? The three preferences set one another off. Zhou’s question looks for kindred spirits and conveys the feeling that they are hard to find.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.4c013908d903: Mix in paper ash. Coat the plate.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.b6bff1098f32: 禽兽之变诈几何哉? 止增笑耳. A rhetorical question and a clipped judgment turn suspense into mockery.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.c09933c4e841: Offer to buy a horse and its gear for this purpose. 市 is “buy.”
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.01c55d9e139d: 其人舍然大喜, 晓之者亦舍然大喜. The same phrase shows relief on both sides. It echoes and reverses the opening distress.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.82fcc0f25553: Explain something so that he understands. You.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.c39297c92b5c: 斯是陋室, 惟吾德馨. Immortals give mountains renown and dragons give waters wonder. The resident’s character does similar work for the room, connecting the images, people and activities that follow.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.39bd760e8936: Very many. Washed by clear rippling water.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.bdf84bd9e994: Textbook forms include 愿驰千里足, 对镜帖花黄, 火伴 and 双兔. Some witnesses read 愿借明驼千里足, 贴, 伙伴 or 两兔. Copy the forms in the text when practicing dictation.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.ff62cd13b11a: 将军百战死, 壮士十年归. The two lines complete each other, 互文. Officers and soldiers share both kinds of fate. A long war fits into a single couplet.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.6da4ba04626e: A man from the state of Qi, 杞, worried that heaven and earth might collapse, leaving him nowhere to live. His worry kept him from sleeping or eating.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.e319be209325: Received text possibly Jin. The story comes from “Heaven’s Gifts”, 天瑞, in the Liezi, traditionally attributed to Lie Yukou. The received book may date to the Jin period. Qi, 杞, is the small ancient state in the story.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.c08debea2d8c: 卿言多务, 孰若孤? Sun repeats Lü Meng’s reason for putting off study, then answers it with a question and his own experience.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.9be2ffd8fabd: In the book title, 论 is pronounced lún.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.f61c6949395f: Follow close behind. Give chase together.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.f60d6ffc75af: Repeated sighs in the textbook reading. The loom and its shuttle.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.49d471983b3f: Question one of two. Why mention the basket, ladle and shabby lane?
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.6f3b9c23b75b: The flow erodes a hollow. Go against the current.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.06d55c9585ba: 吾穿井得一人. The words “gain a person” leave out “the use of.” The wording survives as it spreads while its meaning shifts. That ambiguity drives the plot.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.2b79e2fd5921: Cloudlike hair at the temples. Apply a yellow face decoration. 帖 is read as 贴.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.960e0cc3283e: 苔痕上阶绿, 草色入帘青. The verbs “climb” and “enter” give still greenery motion. The green links the steps and curtained room in a quiet scene.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.59c49b0d802e: 溉 means irrigate. 汲 means draw water.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.085f47bd5756: The textbook credits the Tang poet and essayist Liu Yuxi. A ming, 铭, was an inscription that could praise a deed or remind one how to live. This one uses rhyme and balanced lines to give a plain room an ethical meaning.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.9ccf42622b16: Question one of two. Which pair frames the emotional change in “The Man from Qi”?
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.ad1d8436aca3: 友人惭, 下车引之. 元方入门不顾. Actions carry the ending. The friend’s anger turns to shame, and Yuanfang’s departure leaves readers space to discuss courtesy.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.d0af342ceacb: In anger — ladle or pour oil.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.463ea9524b82: A little while — its eyes seemed shut.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.2b3188769206: Hit eight or nine of ten shots — give a nod.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.23249d75e07f: At the river — like this flowing water. 夫 gives the ending an exclamatory tone.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.de47236a59b1: The iron frame that holds the type — hold the assembly near a fire to heat it.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.5f364420c4d4: 薄如钱唇, 每字为一印. A familiar coin rim conveys the thinness. A separate piece for each character makes a fresh arrangement possible.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.9b4854f2cc57: Be fond of it — take delight in it.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.d341606069ee: Put on the old clothes. 裳 historically refers to a lower garment.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.346ee6af752c: The received “Upright Conduct” text also punctuates 期日中 and the next clause with a comma. The textbook comparison copy uses a full stop after 期日中.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.cb134e82ea41: A block-printed edition — the thin rim of a coin.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.b54bf1f7b33f: Northern Song thinker Zhou Dunyi, from Yingdao in what is now Dao County, Hunan, contrasts three flowers. A shuo, 说, is a short discourse that develops a point. Here the lotus stands for the junzi, 君子, a person of cultivated character.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.5eb5e55e5840: Older sister — support each other as they walk.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.8a42242e6817: 更互用之, 瞬息可就. The steps run from making type to setting it to printing. The two-plate system shows how typesetting and printing can proceed in parallel.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.3c1f425c626d: Unit four. A Letter of Advice to My Son
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.4b6fcbdd2d69: Show a model answer. In the first line, 若 is the pronoun “you.” In the second, 不若 means “less good than.”
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.6071ab0f3b1f: Qi is the name of an ancient state. 亡 stands for 无, “to lack.”
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.31328207a1c6: The textbook has 骨已尽矣 and keeps a comma before 而. The Wikisource text has 骨已尽 and gives 径 as 迳.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.b8f9b34dd241: This anonymous narrative yuefu ballad comes from the Northern Dynasties tradition and is preserved in Guo Maoqian’s Song collection Yuefu Poems, juan twenty-five. Yuefu, yuèfǔ, was originally a music bureau and became a name for a verse tradition. The poem gives Mulan a story, while historical evidence leaves her identity and hometown uncertain.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.fe5e2a75f428: Play a plain qin zither — Buddhist scriptures.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.dda65cfd0b7c: Lost or confused — left in doubt or on insecure ground.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.5c76e80bf5a5: Military action — cold northern air — a metal instrument used to sound the time on night watch.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.062d566853b0: Question one of two. When does the butcher understand the purpose of the first wolf’s act?
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.5e2c482d31e6: The textbook reads 世人甚爱牡丹, while the linked classical text has 世人盛愛牡丹.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.c37c51ee0ea4: Label with paper — store in wooden compartments.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.d6e55266882b: Read broadly and selectively — learn about historical events.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.897384acfd74: Question one of two. Why keep several pieces of the same character?
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.c62b88788027: Question one of twelve. How can readers tell Lü Meng has changed, even though the text skips over his study sessions?
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.9c09b0d0e499: Unit six. Digging a Well “Gains a Man”. The Man Who Feared the Sky Would Fall
yuwen/yw-wenyan-7.be2896cd3847: Look at someone with fresh eyes. 更 means anew here.

yuwen/yw-wenyan-basics.cb5762ef8048: The Analects, 论语, record the sayings of Confucius and his students, collected by later students. Confucius, also called 孔子, lived from five hundred fifty-one to four hundred seventy-nine B C E. Twenty books; a Confucian classic. 子曰 equals “The Master said”.

An official writes that a leader should "worry before everyone else worries, and be happy only after everyone else is happy." Nearly every middle-schooler in China can recite these five texts. Can you crack them?

yuwen/yw-wenyan-classics.d84df4beefab: Tao Yuanming, 陶渊明, quit his official job to farm and write. He lived from about three hundred sixty-five to four hundred twenty-seven. In this story a fisherman from Wuling, 武陵, finds a hidden village whose people fled the wars of the Qin dynasty — about six hundred years earlier — and never left. Wuling is around today's Changde, Hunan.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-classics.e74f573dfa78: US link: compare Thomas More's Utopia with Peach Blossom Spring — both imagine a perfect society to criticise the real one. Utopia dates to fifteen sixteen.
yuwen/yw-wenyan-classics.522c1e921cda: Peach Blossom Spring is Tao Yuanming's imagined ideal society — no war, no oppression, everyone living in peace. "They got lost and never found the road again" tells us such a place doesn't exist in real life. Tao lived through civil wars; the story shows his dream of a better life and his criticism of his own times. Tao lived from about three hundred sixty-five to four hundred twenty-seven.

yuwen/yw-writing.6219f338749d: "Phoenix head, leopard tail", 凤头豹尾: open as beautifully as a phoenix's head, end as powerfully as a leopard's tail. Flip through the technique cards, then identify the techniques in famous and model openings and endings — eight of ten completes the mission.
yuwen/yw-writing.1a7041a5805c: Don't mix up: Flashback-first, 倒叙, doesn't mean writing the whole essay backwards: you show the ending or the most memorable moment first, then go back and tell it in order. An inserted flashback, 插叙, is a memory dropped into the middle — afterwards you return to the main line.

yuwen/yw-writing.ec177c19cbcb: "妈妈很累", Mom is tired — five characters, and the reader sees nothing. "她把最后一个碗放进柜子, 一只手扶着腰, 慢慢直起身", She puts the last bowl in the cupboard, one hand on her lower back, and slowly straightens up — now we see it. In ELA this is called "show, don't tell." In the 中考 the essay is usually worth around fifty points, a third or more of the whole Chinese exam — and the high marks hide in details like these.

_shared.c3f84a45b031: Fort McPherson. Today: Tyler Perry Studios, Atlanta. An Army post in southwest Atlanta for more than one hundred twenty years; in World War One it held German prisoners of war. After it closed in twenty eleven, much of the land became Tyler Perry Studios.
_shared.c190ed97c8c0: Leshan Giant Buddha. Today: Leshan, Sichuan. Seventy-one meters tall, carved into a cliff where three rivers meet — it took ninety years. Its ears are about seven meters long.
_shared.db2a42bf9f2e: Yingtian. Today: Nanjing, Jiangsu. Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming at Yingtian and built a city wall over thirty-five kilometers long — much of it still stands. In fourteen twenty-one the capital moved to Beijing.
_shared.081fa5a13fd2: Warm Springs. Spring water comes out of the ground here at about eighty-eight degrees Fahrenheit, thirty-one degrees Celsius. Franklin D. Roosevelt first came in nineteen twenty-four hoping the warm pools would help his legs after polio, built his Little White House here, and died here on April twelfth, nineteen forty-five; nearby FDR State Park was built by the CCC.
_shared.8f7c33627361: Irwinville. At dawn on May tenth, eighteen sixty-five, Union cavalry surprised the camp of Confederate President Jefferson Davis, who had fled south after Richmond fell. The spot is now a small state historic site in the pine woods.
_shared.36fbae364809: Appalachian Trail. A footpath of about two thousand two hundred miles from Springer Mountain in Georgia to Mount Katahdin in Maine. Hikers who walk the whole trail usually take five to seven months, following white paint blazes on trees and rocks.
_shared.6fd5a7082ba3: Springfield, Missouri. In January and February eighteen thirty-nine, Trail of Tears groups passed here as they pushed west across the Ozarks in midwinter. Today it is Missouri’s third-largest city.
_shared.9d9bf741927a: New Spain. Today: Mexico and the US Southwest. Spain’s empire in North America stretched from Central America to today’s California and Texas, ruled from Mexico City. It ended when Mexico won its independence in eighteen twenty-one.
_shared.8ffdd66d26ee: Buffalo. A city at the eastern end of Lake Erie and the western end of the Erie Canal. After eighteen twenty-five, shipping goods from Buffalo to New York City became about ninety percent cheaper, and the small village boomed; Niagara Falls is only about twenty miles away.
_shared.94b332653910: Yueyang Tower. Today: Yueyang, Hunan. A three-storey wooden tower on the city wall above Dongting Lake. Fan Zhongyan wrote “先天下之忧而忧, 后天下之乐而乐” for it — without ever climbing it himself.
_shared.fcde51d3d947: South Carolina. Today: South Carolina, and North Carolina. Georgia was founded as a buffer to protect rich English Carolina, where enslaved Africans — most of the people — grew rice and indigo. In December eighteen sixty South Carolina became the first state to leave the Union.
_shared.695985697ce4: Nuuk. The capital of Greenland and its biggest town, with about twenty thousand people on the ice-free south-west coast.
_shared.8fd1a6093e95: Providence Canyon. “Georgia’s Little Grand Canyon” is not ancient at all: its gullies, up to about one hundred fifty feet deep, formed in the eighteen hundreds when poor farming let rain wash the soil away. The walls are striped pink, orange, red and purple.
_shared.665d0428d2d2: Fayetteville. A small city south of Atlanta that became a movie-making center after Georgia began giving film companies tax credits of up to thirty percent in two thousand eight. Huge sound stages at Trilith Studios have hosted Marvel superhero movies — people joke about “Y’allywood”.
_shared.e2e6675c16b5: The Dalles. Here the wagon road ended at the Columbia River. Families either built rafts to float their wagons through the dangerous rapids or, after eighteen forty-six, paid a toll to take the Barlow Road around Mount Hood.
_shared.dcb63c71ebd4: Chichén Itzá. A great Maya city on Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula. Its step pyramid, El Castillo, has three hundred sixty-five steps — one for each day of the year.
_shared.40f8d0d7a2bc: Georgia Aquarium. One of the largest aquariums in the world, it opened in two thousand five next to Centennial Olympic Park. Visitors walk through a glass tunnel while whale sharks — the biggest fish on Earth — glide overhead.
_shared.ac90ab9d9257: FAST, China Sky Eye. Today: Pingtang County, Guizhou. A radio telescope five hundred meters across, built in a natural bowl among karst hills — the largest single-dish radio telescope in the world. It has found hundreds of new pulsars.
_shared.5104a74c686c: Georgia State Capitol. Home of the General Assembly and the governor’s office, its dome is covered in real gold leaf from Dahlonega. In nineteen fifty-six lawmakers here added the Confederate battle flag to the state flag; it was finally replaced in two thousand one and two thousand three.
_shared.f32437867f06: Sierra Nevada. A wall of granite mountains along eastern California. Thousands of Chinese workers blasted fifteen tunnels through it for the Central Pacific, sometimes gaining only about a foot a day, and kept working through winters of deep snow.
_shared.f93e3a16c92f: Osaka. Japan’s second big city region, a port and trading city for over one thousand years, squeezed onto a narrow coastal plain.
_shared.4ad14d25edde: Kinderdijk. Nineteen windmills built in the seventeen hundreds to pump water off the low fields of the Netherlands, about a quarter of which lies below sea level.
_shared.e4306a3bfdb9: Coosa. Today: Under Carters Lake, Murray County. Coosa was the main town of a chiefdom whose power reached into Tennessee and Alabama. When de Soto arrived on July sixteenth, fifteen forty, he took its chief hostage; the town site now lies under the waters of Carters Lake.
_shared.b8356e09bc2b: Medina. Muhammad and his followers moved here from Mecca in six twenty-two — year one of the Islamic calendar. His tomb is in the Prophet’s Mosque.
_shared.d5dcd74a91db: Rhine River. It flows about one thousand two hundred thirty kilometers from the Alps to the North Sea through Switzerland, Germany and the Netherlands — Europe’s busiest shipping river.
_shared.439bc77056a5: Albany. In nineteen sixty-one to nineteen sixty-two the Albany Movement protested segregation across this whole Coastal Plain city: more than one thousand people were jailed, including Dr. King, and its freedom songs spread across the nation. The Albany Civil Rights Institute tells the story today.
_shared.57e4b67078aa: Thomas County Courthouse. The elected county commissioners of Thomas County meet here to decide on roads, budgets and other county business. The courthouse itself dates from eighteen fifty-eight.
_shared.7fcb89272afd: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park. Along a few blocks of Auburn Avenue you can visit the house where King was born at five oh one Auburn Avenue, Ebenezer Baptist Church, and the King Center. Dr. King and Coretta Scott King rest in a white tomb in the middle of a reflecting pool.
_shared.a1a99baba754: Ganges River. A sacred river for Hindus, about two thousand five hundred kilometers long. The Buddha taught, and great Indian empires grew, in the Ganges plain.
_shared.d69ae91b35f6: Arizona. A desert state in the Southwest, home of the Grand Canyon and of the Navajo Nation, the largest Native American reservation in the US. Its southern strip was bought from Mexico in the Gadsden Purchase of eighteen fifty-three.
_shared.ac7006ca434a: Altamaha River. Formed where the Ocmulgee and Oconee rivers meet, it is one of the biggest rivers on the East Coast and runs free with no dams. It was colonial Georgia’s southern frontier; Highland Scots built Darien near its mouth in seventeen thirty-six.
_shared.8fedec7ddd41: Taipei. Taipei lies in a basin in northern Taiwan. Its five-hundred-eight-meter Taipei one oh one tower was once the tallest building in the world.
_shared.c0b967aab323: Gadsden Purchase. Today: southern Arizona and New Mexico. In eighteen fifty-three the US paid Mexico ten million dollars for this strip of desert south of the Gila River, because it offered the flattest route for a railroad to California. It completed the outline of the lower forty-eight states.
_shared.9b22b65d2be3: Trinity site. Today: White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico. At five twenty-nine a.m. on the sixteenth of July, nineteen forty-five, Manhattan Project scientists exploded the first atomic bomb in this New Mexico desert. The flash lit up the sky for many miles around, and the heat melted the sand into a green glass now called trinitite. The site is open to visitors only on a few days a year.
_shared.567f15008fbe: Yushu. Today: Yushu, Qinghai. A Tibetan town about three thousand seven hundred meters high in the Sanjiangyuan area.
_shared.d21623f8fa59: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum. Today: Purple Mountain, Nanjing. Visitors climb three hundred ninety-two steps to reach Sun Yat-sen’s tomb on Purple Mountain. From above, the layout looks like a bell — a call to wake people up.
_shared.273e4c962228: Huntsville. At Redstone Arsenal, Wernher von Braun’s rocket team built the rocket that launched Explorer One, America’s first satellite, in nineteen fifty-eight, and NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center here developed the Saturn Five Moon rocket. A real Saturn Five now lies on its side at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center, home of Space Camp.
_shared.3143b20b2f44: Chicago Board of Trade Building. A nineteen thirty skyscraper in Chicago where traders buy and sell contracts for corn, wheat and soybeans. A statue of Ceres, goddess of grain, stands on top.
_shared.a56469af64a8: Oregon. Today’s state is just the southwestern part of the old Oregon Country; it became the thirty-third state in eighteen fifty-nine. Its first state constitution even tried to ban Black people from moving there — a law not fully removed until nineteen twenty-six.
_shared.1d31ea3502c7: Denver. The “Mile-High City” at the foot of the Rocky Mountains in Colorado, exactly one mile above sea level, or one thousand six hundred nine meters.
_shared.84403b5df4de: Southern colonies. Warm weather and a long growing season made planters rich from tobacco, rice and indigo. That wealth came from the forced labor of enslaved Africans — about four in every ten people here were enslaved by seventeen seventy.
_shared.d62bf7025015: Susa. Today: Shush, Iran. One of the oldest cities in the world and a capital of the Persian kings. Royal messengers rode two thousand five hundred kilometers from Sardis to Susa in about a week.
_shared.1291d7d94c0e: Tallulah Gorge. A gorge about three hundred meters deep in north-east Georgia, cut by the Tallulah River. A suspension bridge swings over it.
_shared.ce44b3ad7652: Thermopylae. A narrow path between mountains and the sea. King Leonidas and his three hundred Spartans held off the huge Persian army here for three days.
_shared.3870953bb407: Jingyang Ridge. Today: Yanggu County, Shandong. A low ridge in western Shandong where, in the novel, Wu Song kills a tiger with his bare hands after eighteen bowls of wine. Today it is a park with a tiger statue.
_shared.c64ad54ddcee: Mount Qomolangma, Everest. On the China-Nepal border. Its height was measured again in twenty twenty by Chinese and Nepali surveyors: eight thousand eight hundred forty-eight point eight six meters.
_shared.0a739e40fc2a: Strait of Magellan. A twisting, stormy channel between South America and Tierra del Fuego. Magellan’s ships needed thirty-eight days to get through to the Pacific.
_shared.3e9fa68c5c77: Maldives. About one thousand two hundred tiny coral islands in the Indian Ocean. Most land is less than one point five meters above the sea, so rising seas are a real danger.
_shared.e2cb4b2e3784: Gaocheng Observatory, Dengfeng. Today: Dengfeng, Henan. A brick tower used to measure the sun’s shadow. Guo Shoujing’s calendar fixed the year at three hundred sixty-five point two four two five days.
_shared.55a0a26098c6: Richmond. Henry Kaiser’s four shipyards in Richmond, California, built seven hundred forty-seven ships for World War Two — one Liberty ship was put together in under five days. Thousands of women “Rosies” and Black workers from the South worked here; today it is the Rosie the Riveter, World War Two Home Front National Historical Park.
_shared.018c7253658f: Suwannee River. The Suwannee begins in the Okefenokee Swamp and winds about two hundred forty miles south through Florida to the Gulf of Mexico. Tannins from swamp plants stain its water the color of tea, and it is the river in Florida’s state song, “Old Folks at Home.”
